title: 02 Day Training of Functionaries of Senior Citizen Home
location: YMA Hall, Yma hall P&E veng, Serchhip, Mizoram
descriptionHtml:
Venue: YMA Hall, Serchhip, Mizoram
Date: 27–28 February 2026

 

The 02-Day Training of Functionaries of Senior Citizen Home was successfully conducted at YMA Hall, Serchhip, Mizoram on 27–28 February 2026. The programme was organized with the objective of strengthening the knowledge, skills, and capacities of staff and caregivers working in senior citizen homes to ensure quality care and effective management of elderly services.

 

Day 1: Inaugural Session and Technical Sessions

The training programme commenced with an inaugural session, where the organizers welcomed the participants and highlighted the importance of professional caregiving and proper management practices in senior citizen homes. The resource persons emphasized the growing needs of the elderly population and the responsibility of institutions to provide safe, dignified, and compassionate care. 

Technical sessions on the first day focused on:

  • Concept and importance of institutional care for older persons
  • Roles and responsibilities of functionaries in senior citizen homes
  • Basic health care, hygiene, nutrition, and medication management
  • Communication skills and psychosocial support for the elderly

Interactive discussions and experience-sharing enabled participants to understand practical challenges faced in caregiving and management. 

 

Day 2: Practical Learning and Management Aspects

The second day of the training emphasized practical approaches and administrative aspects of running senior citizen homes effectively. Sessions covered:

  • Standardization and quality assurance in elderly care services
  • Record keeping, documentation, and reporting systems
  • Safety, emergency preparedness, and referral linkages
  • Recreational activities, mental health promotion, and active ageing initiatives

Group activities and case study discussions were conducted to enhance learning and teamwork among participants. The training concluded with a feedback session where participants shared their views and appreciated the usefulness of the programme. 

 

Participation

The training was attended by functionaries, caregivers, and representatives from various senior citizen homes and community-based organizations in and around Serchhip district. The active participation and enthusiasm of the trainees contributed to the overall success of the programme. 

 

Conclusion

The two-day training programme proved to be informative and capacity-building in nature. It helped participants gain better understanding of elderly care standards, management practices, and the importance of providing holistic support to senior citizens. Such initiatives are expected to improve the quality of services delivered in senior citizen homes and promote dignity and well-being among the elderly population.

title: 02 Day Training of Functionaries of Senior Citizen Home
location: MFM Hall, Durtlang, Aizawl, Mizoram, Aizawl, Mizoram
descriptionHtml:
02 Day Training of Functionaries of Senior Citizen Home

 

Programme Information

  • Venue: MFM Hall
  • Date: 9th –10th February 2026
  • Participants: Functionaries, caregivers and staff of Senior Citizen Homes

Background 

The two-day training programme was organized to strengthen the knowledge and skills of personnel involved in the management and caregiving services of senior citizen homes. With the increasing need for quality elderly care services, the programme aimed to equip participants with practical understanding on institutional management, caregiving practices and psychosocial support for older persons.

 

Activities Conducted 

During the programme, resource persons conducted sessions on various aspects of elderly care and institutional management. The sessions focused on improving participants’ understanding of the physical, emotional and social needs of senior citizens residing in care homes.

The major activities included:

  • Orientation on elderly care and active ageing
  • Sessions on health care, hygiene and nutrition for senior citizens
  • Discussions on communication skills and emotional support
  • Guidance on documentation, reporting and record maintenance
  • Awareness on safety measures and emergency preparedness
  • Group discussions and sharing of field experiences

Interactive participation and practical discussions helped participants gain better clarity on challenges faced in caregiving and methods to improve the quality of services in senior citizen homes.

 

Resource Persons 

Experienced professionals and subject experts from the field of social welfare and elderly care facilitated the sessions and interacted with participants throughout the training programme.

 

Key Outcomes 

The programme resulted in:

  • Enhanced knowledge and caregiving skills among participants
  • Better understanding of institutional management practices
  • Increased awareness regarding dignity, safety and well-being of senior citizens
  • Improved confidence among caregivers in handling elderly-related issues

Feedback from Participants 

Participants expressed satisfaction with the content and methodology of the training programme. They appreciated the practical nature of the sessions and highlighted the usefulness of the programme in improving their day-to-day caregiving responsibilities.

 

Conclusion 

The 02-Day Training of Functionaries of Senior Citizen Home was successfully conducted and achieved its intended objectives. The programme contributed towards strengthening the capacity of caregivers and promoting quality care services for elderly persons residing in institutional settings.

title: 03 Day Programme for Dementia Care & Management
location: Bethlehem Venglai Hall Aizawl Mizoram, Bethlehem Aizawl Mizoram, Aizawl, Mizoram
descriptionHtml:
Organized by: RRTC, Mission Foundation Movement

Date: 5th February – 7th February 2026

Venue: Bethlehem Venglai Hall, Aizawl

Total Participants: 40

Chief Guest: Mr. C. Lalsawivunga, Hon’ble Minister, Art & Culture Department, etc.

 

1. Introduction

A programme on Dementia Care & Management was organized by RRTC, Mission Foundation Movement on 5th February-7th February 2026 at Bethlehem Venglai Hall, Aizawl, Mizoram. The programme aimed to raise awareness about dementia, improve caregiving skills, and promote better support systems for elderly persons suffering from cognitive disorders.

Dementia has become an increasing concern worldwide, particularly among the ageing population. In communities where family members are the primary caregivers, it is important to equip them with proper knowledge and skills to care for persons living with dementia. The programme brought together community members, caregivers, social workers, and health professionals to discuss practical approaches for dementia care and management.

 

2. Inaugural Session

The programme began with an inaugural session attended by distinguished guests, participants, and organizers. The programme was graced by Chief Guest C. Lalsawivunga, Hon’ble Minister, Art & Culture Department, Government of Mizoram.

In his address, the Chief Guest highlighted the importance of caring for elderly citizens and emphasized the need for community awareness regarding dementia. He acknowledged the efforts of RRTC, Mission Foundation Movement in organizing programmes that promote the welfare and dignity of senior citizens. He also encouraged families and communities to provide compassionate care and support to elderly persons living with dementia.

 

3. Objectives of the Programme

The main objectives of the programme were:

  • To increase public awareness about dementia and its impact
  • To educate caregivers and community members on dementia care
  • To promote early detection and management of dementia
  • To strengthen community support for elderly persons
  • To encourage better caregiving practices for persons living with dementia

4. Participants

The programme witnessed the participation of caregivers, elderly persons, community leaders, NGO representatives, and social workers. Participants actively engaged in discussions and shared their experiences regarding elderly care and dementia-related challenges.

 

5. Programme Sessions

The programme included several informative sessions covering important aspects of dementia care and management.

Understanding Dementia

The session introduced participants to dementia, including its causes, symptoms, and stages. Participants learned about the difference between normal ageing and dementia, as well as the importance of early recognition.

Caregiving Techniques

This session focused on practical caregiving approaches such as:

  • Effective communication with dementia patients
  • Managing behavioural and psychological symptoms
  • Creating a safe and supportive environment for elderly persons

Participants were encouraged to share their caregiving experiences and challenges.

Community Support and Awareness

Another important session highlighted the role of families, communities, and local organizations in supporting dementia patients. Participants were informed about the importance of empathy, patience, and community cooperation in caring for elderly individuals.

 

6. Key Highlights

  • Valuable insights shared by experts on dementia care
  • Interactive discussions among participants
  • Increased awareness regarding dementia and elderly care
  • Encouragement of community-based support systems

7. Outcome of the Programme

The programme successfully increased awareness and understanding of dementia among participants. It also helped strengthen the knowledge and capacity of caregivers and community members to support persons living with dementia.

Participants expressed appreciation for the informative sessions and highlighted the need for more such awareness programmes in the future.

 

8. Conclusion

The programme on Dementia Care & Management organized by RRTC, Mission Foundation Movement was successful in achieving its objectives. The presence of the Hon’ble Chief Guest added significance to the event and encouraged greater attention toward issues affecting the elderly population.

The programme contributed to improving awareness, strengthening caregiving practices, and promoting a compassionate approach to dementia care within the community.

title: 03 Day Programme for Dementia Care & Management
location: L three hall, L 3 Hall, Lawngtlai, Lawngtlai, Mizoram
descriptionHtml:
Overview

RRTC, Mission Foundation Movement successfully organized a three-day training programme on Dementia Care & Management at Lawngtlai, Mizoram from 19th – 21st February 2026. The programme was conducted with the aim of strengthening knowledge and caregiving capacity among community members, health workers, and caregivers of elderly persons.

 

With the steady rise in the ageing population, dementia has emerged as an important health and social concern. The training programme focused on enhancing awareness, promoting early identification of symptoms, and equipping participants with practical caregiving skills to improve the quality of life of persons living with dementia.

 

Purpose of the Programme

The programme was organized to achieve the following purposes:

  • To enhance understanding of dementia and related conditions 
  • To build skills in caring for elderly persons with cognitive impairment 
  • To promote early diagnosis and appropriate intervention 
  • To encourage community-based support systems for dementia care 
  • To reduce stigma and misconceptions related to mental decline in old age 

Participation

The training programme was attended by caregivers, community volunteers, health functionaries, representatives of local organizations, and family members of elderly persons. Participants showed keen interest and actively took part in discussions, group work, and practical sessions conducted during the programme.

 

Programme Implementation

 

Day 1: Awareness and Basic Understanding

The first day focused on creating awareness and providing foundational knowledge about dementia. Sessions covered the definition, causes, symptoms, stages, and risk factors associated with dementia. Participants were also informed about the difference between normal ageing and dementia-related conditions. Interactive discussions enabled participants to clarify doubts and share their experiences

Day 2: Caregiving Skills and Management

The second day concentrated on practical aspects of caregiving. Resource persons explained various approaches to managing behavioural changes, communication difficulties, and daily care needs of dementia patients. Demonstrations were conducted on safe mobility practices, maintaining hygiene, and ensuring proper nutrition for elderly persons.

Participants were also sensitized about the emotional and psychological needs of persons living with dementia and the importance of patience and empathy in caregiving.

Day 3: Community Role and Support Mechanisms

The final day emphasized the role of families, communities, and local institutions in providing continuous care and support to elderly persons with dementia. Sessions highlighted caregiver stress management, importance of social inclusion, and available welfare schemes and services for senior citizens.

The programme concluded with an interactive feedback session, where participants expressed appreciation for the knowledge gained and suggested the need for more such training programmes in rural areas.

 

Training Methodology

The programme adopted participatory and learner-friendly methods such as:

  • Lecture-cum-discussion Demonstrations 
  • Group activities 
  • Experience sharing 
  • Question and answer sessions 

These approaches ensured better understanding and practical learning among participants.
 

Outcomes and Impact

The programme contributed significantly to improving awareness and caregiving capacity at the community level. Participants reported increased confidence in identifying early signs of dementia and providing appropriate care to affected elderly persons.

The training also helped in promoting positive attitudes towards ageing and encouraged the formation of informal support networks among caregivers.

 

Conclusion

The three-day training programme on Dementia Care & Management organized at Lawngtlai was successfully completed and achieved its intended objectives. The initiative strengthened community knowledge, enhanced caregiving skills, and promoted a compassionate approach towards elderly persons living with dementia.

RRTC, Mission Foundation Movement continues to play an important role in addressing issues related to ageing and dementia through awareness generation and capacity-building programmes.

title: 29th Meeting of the Committee to Review the Implementation of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, and the Protection of Civil Rights (PCR) Act, 1955.
descriptionHtml:
Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment (SJ&E), Dr. Virendra Kumar, and Union Minister for Tribal Affairs (TA), Shri Jual Oram, co-chaired the 29th meeting of the Committee to review the implementation of the Protection of the Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and to devise ways and means to curb offences of Untouchability and Atrocities against SCs and STs, at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi today.

Union Minister of State, Ministry of Tribal Affairs Shri Durga Das Uikey, Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary Department of Social Justice & Empowerment, Shri Gudey Srinivas, Secretary NCSC and Shri Prashant Kumar Singh, Secretary, NCST, non-official members Dr. K. Muniyappa Obdenahalli and Ms. Sukeshi Oram and Shri Sanjiv Pandey, Member Secretary NALSA was also present. Additional Chief Secretaries, Principal Secretaries/Secretaries of the SC/ST Development/Welfare Department, Home Department and Senior Police officials from 20 States/UTs attended the meeting.

During the meeting, detailed discussions were held on key aspects, including the rate of filing of charge sheets in courts, pendency of cases, status of establishment of Exclusive Special Courts and Special Police Stations, conduct of Vigilance and Monitoring Committee meetings, pendency of grievances registered on the National Helpline Against Atrocities, and awareness generation initiatives. The implementation of the PCR and PoA Acts was comprehensively reviewed, along with the formulation of action plans to address identified gaps and shortcomings. The Committee reaffirmed the Government’s firm resolve to ensure dignity, justice, and protection for all vulnerable sections of society.

The Union Minister, Dr. Virendra Kumar, in his concluding remarks, stressed the need for regular conduct of State-level and District-level Vigilance and Monitoring Committee meetings to effectively review the implementation of the provisions of the Act across States and Union Territories. He directed State/UT officers to undertake proactive measures to ensure that members of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes are not subjected to exploitation. Additionally, he emphasized the adoption of effective preventive measures to reduce incidents of atrocities and untouchability, thereby fostering a sense of equality, dignity and social harmony across States and UTs.

He further stressed the importance of increasing the number of Special Police Stations to strengthen accountability and ensure prompt action against erring officials, in accordance with the provisions of the PoA Act, in cases of neglect of duty.

Union Minister of Tribal Affairs, Shri Jual Oram, emphasized the need to organize meetings at multiple locations across the country to sensitize stakeholders and create wider public awareness about the rights of beneficiaries and the provisions of the law. He also highlighted the importance of leveraging technology, particularly through the development of an IT-based platform, to enable robust data analysis and strengthen monitoring and implementation mechanisms.

The Minister of State for Tribal Affairs, Shri Durgadas Uikey, addressed the meeting and highlighted the importance of conducting regular review meetings. He drew attention to critical concerns such as non-implementation of statutory directions and the need to enhance awareness initiatives to ensure effective implementation of the relevant Acts and schemes.

The meeting concluded with a commitment from all participants to uphold the intent and spirit of these crucial Acts and to ensure timely and effective justice for victims of caste-based discrimination and atrocities.

title: Academic Visit of Students from LNCT University to Dr. Ambedkar International Centre and Dr. Ambedkar National Memorial
Activities of productive ageing
location: Positron Institute Deythang, Rinchenpong Gyalshng District, Soreng, Sikkim
descriptionHtml:
1. Introduction
This report presents the successful implementation and completion of the Training Programme on Bamboo Utility Handicraft Assembler for Senior Citizens, conducted at Positron Institute, Deythang, Rinchenpong Constituency, Soreng District, Sikkim. The programme was organized under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, and sponsored by the Women, Child, Senior Citizen and Divyangjan Welfare Department, Government of Sikkim. The training was implemented through the State Institute of Capacity Building (SICB) under the Skill Development Department, Government of Sikkim.
The training programme was conducted from 11th January 2026 to 16th March 2026 with the objective of strengthening traditional bamboo craftsmanship among senior citizens and providing them with meaningful skill-based engagement opportunities. The curriculum focused on hands-on practical training in bamboo cutting, splitting, weaving, assembling, shaping, and finishing of bamboo utility products. Through this structured approach, participants developed both basic and advanced skills required for producing functional bamboo handicraft items.
The primary aim of the programme was to empower senior citizens, a group often excluded from mainstream skill development initiatives, by equipping them with practical vocational skills that encourage self-reliance, creativity, and opportunities for supplemental income generation. Participants were trained in producing various bamboo utility items such as baskets, trays, holders, mats, and household products, while also learning about safe tool handling, product finishing, and basic entrepreneurial concepts.
Bamboo, being a traditional and locally available resource in Sikkim, offers significant potential for sustainable livelihood promotion and preservation of indigenous craftsmanship. Recognizing this potential, the programme sought to revive traditional bamboo craft practices while engaging senior citizens in productive and community-oriented activities. Conducting the training at Positron Institute within the local area ensured accessibility for the elderly participants and minimized mobility challenges, thereby encouraging active participation.
The initiative also aligns with the Government of India’s vision of inclusive development, active ageing, and empowerment of senior citizens, as reflected in national welfare frameworks such as the National Action Plan for Senior Citizens (NAPSRC). Through effective collaboration between central and state departments, along with the grassroots-level implementation by Positron Institute, the programme successfully provided an enriching and impactful learning experience to the beneficiaries.
In conclusion, the training programme contributed not only to skill development but also to the social, psychological, and economic well-being of senior citizens in the Rinchenpong region. The positive outcomes of the programme highlight the importance of targeted skill initiatives for elderly populations and demonstrate the potential for replicating similar bamboo-based livelihood programmes across other parts of Sikkim.

2. Objectives
The Training Programme on Bamboo Utility Handicraft Assembler for Senior Citizens was conceptualized with a focused vision to empower elderly beneficiaries from Soreng District by equipping them with practical, culturally rooted, and income-generating skills in bamboo handicraft production. Conducted at the Positron Institute, Deythang, from 11 January 2026 to 16 March 2026, the programme was organised under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, and sponsored by the Women, Child, Senior Citizen and Divyangjan Welfare Department, Government of Sikkim. The programme was implemented through the State Institute of Capacity Building (SICB), functioning under the Skill Development Department, Government of Sikkim, with Positron Institute serving as the training delivery center responsible for curriculum execution, facilitation, and learner support.
The specific objectives of the programme were as follows:
1. To impart practical skills in bamboo utility handicraft making;
The primary objective of the programme was to provide structured, hands-on training to senior citizens in bamboo craft techniques such as cutting, splitting, shaping, weaving, and assembling utility products. The curriculum was carefully designed to help participants develop the ability to produce high-quality, durable bamboo items suitable for household usage, gifting, and local market sale.
2. To promote self-reliance, creativity, and meaningful engagement among senior citizens;
Recognising the importance of active ageing, the programme aimed to engage elderly individuals in productive skill-building activities that enhance their creativity, confidence, and sense of purpose. By learning a culturally relevant craft, participants gained an avenue for continued social participation and personal fulfilment.

3. To create livelihood opportunities through traditional craft-based skills;
The training focused on enabling senior citizens to generate supplementary income through the production and sale of bamboo utility items. Participants were introduced to basic entrepreneurship concepts, including pricing, product finishing, quality control, and local market linkage, thereby encouraging them to explore small-scale home-based enterprises.
4. To preserve and revive traditional bamboo craftsmanship in local communities;
Bamboo craft holds cultural significance in Sikkim. The programme sought to revitalise this traditional skill among the older generation, ensuring its continuity and transfer to younger community members. By strengthening local craftsmanship, the initiative supports sustainable development using eco-friendly and locally available resources.
5. To support inclusive development and active ageing through government-led welfare interventions;
Aligned with the broader goals of AVYAY and national frameworks for senior citizen welfare, the programme aimed to ensure that elderly populations-often overlooked in conventional skill development initiatives-receive access to structured training opportunities. The initiative promotes inclusion, reduces social isolation, and enhances the overall well-being of senior citizens.
In essence, the objectives of the Bamboo Utility Handicraft Assembler training extended beyond the acquisition of craft skills. They were directed toward enhancing dignity, fostering self-dependence, sustaining cultural heritage, and contributing to community-level socio-economic development. Through this intervention, the programme created a meaningful and lasting impact on the lives of senior citizens in the Rinchenpong region.

3. Month-wise Training Activity Details
The Training Programme on Bamboo Utility Handicraft Assembler for Senior Citizens was conducted over a period of two months, from 11th January 2026 to 16th March 2026. The month-wise progress of the training is detailed below, outlining the systematic delivery of practical skills, demonstrations, and hands-on exercises.
3.1. January 2026 – Foundation & Orientation Phase
Duration Covered: 11 January 2026 – 31 January 2026
During the initial phase, trainees were introduced to the basics of bamboo craft, safety practices, and familiarisation with tools. This period focused on building the foundational understanding required for advanced practical work.
Key Activities:
• Inaugural ceremony and orientation session.
•Introduction to bamboo as a raw material (types, qualities, sustainability). 
•Demonstration on bamboo selection, softening, and primary preparation
•Safety instructions for tool handling.
•.Hands-on practice:

Bamboo cutting and trimming.
Splitting and shaping techniques.
Basic weaving patterns.
Introduction to simple product-making (coasters, small mats, and basic
strips).
Learning Outcomes:
Trainees developed confidence in handling bamboo and basic tools.
Understood safety protocols.

Acquired basic shaping and weaving skills

title: Awareness on Health and Wellness session
location: Aizawl, Mizoram, Aizawl, Mizoram, -796005
descriptionHtml:
In celebration of the International Day of Older Persons (IDOP) 2025, supported by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, a programme was organized by the Regional Resource Training Centre (RRTC) at the Synod Conference Centre in Aizawl, Mizoram. The event was conducted with the objective of promoting the well-being, dignity, and active participation of senior citizens in society.

The programme commenced with an inaugural session graced by the Chief Guest, Lalbiakzama, Hon’ble Speaker of the Mizoram Legislative Assembly. In his address, he emphasized the importance of caring for the elderly and acknowledged their invaluable contributions to society. He also highlighted the need for collective efforts from families, communities, and institutions to ensure that senior citizens lead a life of dignity, respect, and security.

The programme featured a variety of activities aimed at awareness, engagement, and empowerment of senior citizens. Key highlights included the administering of pledges to promote respect and care for the elderly, and an awareness session on the National Helpline for Senior Citizens, which informed participants about available support services. A health and wellness session was conducted to educate attendees on maintaining physical and mental health, followed by a customized fitness training session specifically designed for senior citizens to encourage safe and regular physical activity.

In addition, a talk series on ageing with dignity provided valuable insights into emotional well-being, social inclusion, and coping with the challenges of ageing. Cultural engagement was promoted through a folk song competition, allowing participants to showcase their talents and celebrate local traditions. Counselling sessions on healthy lifestyle practices were also organized, offering guidance on nutrition, mental health, and overall well-being.

title: Awareness on Health and Wellness session
location: Synod Conference hall, Aizawl, Mizoram, Aizawl, Mizoram
descriptionHtml:
In celebration of the International Day of Older Persons (IDOP) 2025, supported by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, a programme was organized by the Regional Resource Training Centre (RRTC) at the Synod Conference Centre in Aizawl, Mizoram. The event was conducted with the objective of promoting the well-being, dignity, and active participation of senior citizens in society.

The programme commenced with an inaugural session graced by the Chief Guest, Lalbiakzama, Hon’ble Speaker of the Mizoram Legislative Assembly. In his address, he emphasized the importance of caring for the elderly and acknowledged their invaluable contributions to society. He also highlighted the need for collective efforts from families, communities, and institutions to ensure that senior citizens lead a life of dignity, respect, and security.

The programme featured a variety of activities aimed at awareness, engagement, and empowerment of senior citizens. Key highlights included the administering of pledges to promote respect and care for the elderly, and an awareness session on the National Helpline for Senior Citizens, which informed participants about available support services. A health and wellness session was conducted to educate attendees on maintaining physical and mental health, followed by a customized fitness training session specifically designed for senior citizens to encourage safe and regular physical activity.

In addition, a talk series on ageing with dignity provided valuable insights into emotional well-being, social inclusion, and coping with the challenges of ageing. Cultural engagement was promoted through a folk song competition, allowing participants to showcase their talents and celebrate local traditions. Counselling sessions on healthy lifestyle practices were also organized, offering guidance on nutrition, mental health, and overall well-being.

The programme witnessed an active participation of 245 senior citizens and community members, creating a vibrant, inclusive, and interactive environment. The enthusiastic involvement of participants reflected the relevance and impact of the initiative. The programme concluded successfully with positive feedback from attendees, reaffirming the importance of such events in strengthening awareness, promoting healthy ageing, and fostering a supportive community for senior citizens.

Brief Report on Celebration of International Day of Yog
location: CMIG Premises, 43,Purbalok EM Bypass Kolkata 99, Kolkata, West Bengal
descriptionHtml:
Brief Report on Celebration of International Day of Yoga (IDY) 2026 for Senior Citizens

 

Name of Programme: International Day of Yoga (IDY) 2026 for Senior Citizens

Date: 21 June 2026

Venue: 43, Purbalok, EM Bypass, Kolkata – 99

Organized by: Calcutta Metropolitan Institute of Gerontology: RRTC on Ageing

Total number of Participants: 36 Senior Citizens

 

The International Day of Yoga (IDY) 2026 was observed on 21st June 2026 with enthusiastic participation of senior citizens. The theme of IDY 2026, “Yoga for Healthy Ageing” highlighted the importance of yoga in promoting physical health, mental well-being, active ageing and independence among older adults.

The International Day of Yoga (IDY) 2026 programme for senior citizens was conducted in accordance with the Yoga Protocol (CYP) prescribed by the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India. The session commenced with Prayer and Om Chanting, followed by Loosening Practices (Sukshma Vyayama) to prepare the body for yoga. Participants then performed a series of age-friendly yoga postures, including standing, sitting and supine asanas under the guidance of trained instructors. 

As part of the awareness component of the programme, Dr. Indrani Chakravarty conducted an informative session highlighting the significance of yoga in promoting healthy ageing, physical fitness, mental well-being, stress management, and social engagement among senior citizens. A second interactive session was conducted by Mr. Ipsito Chakravarty, who discussed the holistic benefits of yoga and mindfulness practices for older adults. 

The session further included Pranayama practices such as Kapalabhati (where suitable), Anulom-Vilom and Bhramari to enhance respiratory health and mental well-being. This was followed by Meditation (Dhyana) and concluded with Shanti Path/Prayer, promoting inner peace and holistic wellness. Special care was taken to ensure that all practices were safe, comfortable, and suitable for senior citizens.

A total of 36 senior citizens participated in the programme. The participants actively engaged in the yoga session and expressed their appreciation for the initiative.

title: Celebrating IDOP 2025 Concluding Ceremony
location: Dr Triguna Sen Auditorium, 188 Raja Subodh Chandra Mallick Rd Jadavpur University Campus Area Jadavpur Kolkata, Kolkata, West Bengal
descriptionHtml:
Celebrating IDOP, 2025: Concluding Ceremony

Venue: Dr Triguna Sen Auditorium 188, Raja Subodh Chandra Mallick Rd, Jadavpur University Campus Area, Jadavpur, Kolkata, West Bengal – 700032 

Date: 11th February

Time : 3:00pm – 7:00pm

Synopsis:

CMIG: RRTC on Ageing concluded her year-long celebrations of the IDOP, 2025 by orchestrating a cultural milieu at Dr. Triguna Sen Auditorium, Jadavpur University ,Kolkata on 11th February,2026. The event was uniquely organized to blend entertainment with awareness of elderly issues that the members of Team CMIG have documented from their recent on-field experience. The grand event marked the conclusion of year-long activities that CMIG undertook under the aegis of MSJ&E to celebrate in order to implement the Central Theme of IDOP, 2025. The theme is stated below:

 “Older Persons Driving Local and Global Action: Our Aspirations, Our Well-Being and Our Rights”

The event was participated from distinguished stakeholders in the Geriatric Care, viz., Help Age India, Dignity Foundation and Senior Citizens Welfare Associations. It started as scheduled with Dr. Indrani Chakravarty, Secretary, CMIG delivering the Welcome Address to the coveted gathering. Her speech was accompanied by two consecutive speeches delivered by Mr Shanti Ranjan Chakravarty, President, Executive Committee, CMIG and Mr Ipsito Chakravarty, Project Director of CMIG: RRTC on Ageing. All speakers emphasized on the strategic planning and subsequent on-field implementation of the Central Theme, IDOP, 2025. The academic deliberations were followed by a series of docu dramas, music and pure entertainment meant to enchant the audience and enlighten them about CMIG’s activities in the ongoing financial year. The objective of the program was fulfilled and a clear roadmap has been profiled by CMIG as to the implementation and re-enactment of her programs in the days to come.

title: Celebration of IDOP
location: Zilla Bhawan, Kyongsa Gyalshing, Gyalshing, Sikkim
descriptionHtml:
Report on the Observance of the International Day of
Older Persons at Kyongsa
Gyalshing, December 12 2025
The International Day of Older Persons was observed with due significance at the Conference Hall, Zilla Bhawan, Kyongsa, under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana. The programme was organised by the Women, Child, Senior Citizens & Divyangjan Welfare Department, Gyalshing, with the theme “Older Persons Driving Local and Global Action: Our Aspirations, Our Well-being, Our Rights.”
The District Collector, Gyalshing, Mr. Tenzing D. Denzongpa, graced the occasion as the Chief Guest. The event was attended by Panchayat President, Tikjuk-Kyongsa GPU, Ms. Zangmoo Bhutia, Vice President Mr. Rinchen Namgyal Bhutia, Centre Administrator, One Stop Centre (OSC), Ms. Pema Diki Bhutia, counsellors, case workers, officials of the One Stop Centre, Kyongsa, and senior citizens from the area.
The programme commenced with a welcome address by Case Worker Ms. Bhawana Rai. This was followed by an awareness session on the importance of the International Day of Older Persons and the benefits available under the Protection of Senior Citizens Acts. Advocate and Case Worker Ms. Aita Hangma Limboo elaborated on the roles and responsibilities of the One Stop Centre and the Women Helpline, highlighting various facilities and schemes available for senior citizens in need. She also provided detailed information on legal aid services, tribunal procedures, domestic violence redressal mechanisms, social counselling services, and the five-bedded short-stay facility at the OSC, Kyongsa, attached to the AYUSH Hospital. The gathering was also informed about the Women Helpline Emergency Number 181 for advice, rescue and counselling.
Addressing the gathering, the District Collector expressed his deep respect for senior citizens, acknowledging them as the most experienced and valued members of society whose guidance and wisdom contribute significantly to district development. He briefed the participants on key developmental initiatives in the district, including the proposed Parking Plaza, construction of a Welcome Gate, and the establishment of an SHG Mart. He also voiced concern over the rising cases of suicide and POCSO and sought constructive suggestions from senior citizens to collectively address these social challenges. Emphasising the importance of awareness and utilisation of welfare schemes, he urged older persons to avail themselves of the facilities explained during the programme and assured all possible support from the District Administration.
As a token of love and appreciation, senior citizens Mr. Ganesh Kumar Gurung, Mr. Naksuk Bhutia, Mr. Rinchen Namgyal Bhutia, Mr. Grajaman Subedi, Mr. Namgyal Bhutia, Mr. Bijay Gurung were felicitated for their social work and valuable contributions.
Subsequently, Gender Specialist, District Hub, Mr. Prayash Thapa, briefed the participants on various social security schemes, including the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme, Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY), Ayushman Bharat, and the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP).

location: Auditorium Hall, Namcheybong, Pakyong, Sikkim
descriptionHtml:
Report on the Celebration of the International Day of Older Persons
Under Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana
Pakyong District 26.11.2025
The Women, Child, Senior Citizen and Divyangjan Welfare Department (WCSCDWD), Pakyong District, observed the International Day of Older Persons under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana at the Auditorium Hall of Namcheybong GPU. The programme was headed by DD-cum-SWO, Mrs. Dikit Lepcha.
The event was graced by Mr. Bishal Sharma/Pokhrel, Additional Political Secretary to the Hon’ble Chief Minister and NGO Representative of the District Tribunal for Senior Citizens, as the Chief Guest, and Mr. Thendup Lepcha, SDM (HQ), as the Guest of Honour. Also present were Welfare Officer Mrs. Sunita Dahal, Panchayat President Mrs.Sakeela Rai, Zilla Panchayats, Ward Panchayats, Assistant Directors, officials, staff, senior citizens, and representatives from collaborating organisations.
This year’s theme, “Older Persons Driving Local and Global Action: Our Aspirations, Our Well-Being, Our Rights,” highlighted the vital role of senior citizens in shaping resilient and equitable communities through active participation in local and global decision-making.
Key Highlights of the Programme:
1. Felicitation Ceremony
A total of 10 retired bureaucrats, teachers, and social workers were felicitated for their outstanding contributions and lifelong service to society.
2. Cultural & Motivational Activities
A cake cutting ceremony was organised to uplift the spirits of senior citizens. Gift items were distributed to all participants.
A song dedicated to senior citizens was performed by Ms. Mangalmit Lepcha, a budding singer.
⚫ Mrs. Yasodha Regmi recited poems on the theme of old age, touching the hearts of the audience.
• The programme was successfully anchored by social welfare Inspector. Sesir Ghimirey.
3. Health Support Initiative
A combined medical team from the Health Department and Pakyong PHC conducted comprehensive health check-ups, including:
• Physiotherapy
⚫ Dental screening
• General medical check-up

⚫ Eye check-up
⚫ Nutritional counselling Pharmaceutical support
The team consisted of a Physiotherapist, Dental Surgeon, Medical Officer, Staff Nurse, Dietician, Pharmacist, and Optometrist.
The Greater Lions Club, Siliguri, organised a dedicated eye-screening camp and distributed free spectacles to senior citizens. Additionally, walking sticks were provided as a token of care and support.
4. Technical Session & Awareness
Address by the Chief Guest
The Chief Guest appreciated the department for organising a meaningful programme dedicated to senior citizens. He emphasised:
• The invaluable contributions of older persons
The importance of acknowledging their lifelong service
• The vision of the Hon’ble Chief Minister for a “Sunaulo, Samriddha ani Samarth Sikkim”
• The need to support physical and mental well-being
Collective responsibility in fostering a healthy and addiction-free society
Address by the Deputy Director
DD-cum-SWO Mrs. Dikit Lepcha underlined the significance of observing this day and assured that the department remains accessible for addressing issues faced by senior citizens, especially pension-related matters.
Awareness by Gender Specialist
Ms. Kusum Sharma, Gender Specialist (DHEW), spoke on:
Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) eligibility and necessary documents

Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) improving the quality of life of senior citizens through active ageing, access to basic amenities, and social and financial support
5. Interactive Session
An open discussion was organised where senior citizens shared their concerns and sought clarification on various schemes and provisions. The interaction proved highly productive and encouraging.
Conclusion:
The programme concluded with the Vote of Thanks delivered by Ms. Sanjita Sharma of the DHEW Division. The celebration successfully honored the contributions of senior citizens while promoting awareness on health, welfare schemes, and rights reflecting the district’s commitment to creating a dignified and supportive environment for the elderly.

title: Celebration of IDOP
location: Namchi, Melli Dara GPU, Sikkim
descriptionHtml:
International Day of Older Persons Observed at Melli Dara GPU

 

The International Day of Older Persons, organised by the Women, Child, Senior Citizen and Divyangjan Welfare Department, Namchi District was observed at Melli Dara GPU.

The event centered around the theme, “Older Persons Driving Local and Global Action: Our Aspirations, Our Well-Being, Our Rights,” highlighting the significant contributions of older adults in building resilient and fair societies. It underscored their importance in influencing decisions at both local and global platforms. 

 

MLA/Advisor Melli Constituency, Mr N B Pradhan, in his speech, emphasized that parents must install good values in their children, as this is the foundation for nurturing responsible and respectful individuals. He urged senior citizens to continue contributing to the welfare of their communities. He reminded them that though they are retired they still have the energy and experience to make meaningful contributions. He cited examples of elderly individuals who continue to serve society and encouraged others to follow their lead.

 

He also appealed to the Panchayat members to remain available in their offices so that people can easily access services and resolve their issues. He noted that due to miscommunication, many welfare schemes go unnoticed, and senior citizens often miss out on benefits intended for them. He encouraged all elderly citizens to obtain a senior citizen card to ensure they receive the maximum advantages. He further advised social welfare inspectors to maintain close coordination with the Panchayats so that schemes reach the people they are meant for.

Additionally, he shared information about the Shravan Kumar Puraskar, an award given to children who provide exemplary care and support to their parents. He concluded by encouraging everyone present to cultivate selflessness and continue working for the betterment of society.

 

DC Namchi, Ms Anupa Tamling, in her address, emphasized the importance of protecting and supporting the senior members of society. She noted that while times are changing, it remains essential for older persons to be aware of various schemes and Acts meant for their welfare and protection. She explained that if any issue arises, a written application can be submitted to the DC or SDM office, and the authorities will take necessary action. She assured that the administration is committed to work for the wellbeing of senior citizens.

 

She further highlighted that senior citizens must prioritize their health and should never hesitate to voice their concerns or seek help from the administration. Mental health should be a key focus for every elderly individual. She also spoke about school dropouts and encouraged the retired personnel present to guide and support these youths, whether by helping them develop skills or motivating them to return to school. Such efforts would be a meaningful contribution to society.

 

Additionally, she announced that a comprehensive database of older persons will be created and updated every month, ensuring that the specific needs of each senior citizen are well documented. She also emphasized the importance of issuing senior citizen cards to all eligible individuals so they can fully access the benefits and services meant for them.

 

SWO WCSC&D Namchi, Mr Shyam S Pradhan, in his speech, highlighted the significance of the International Day for Older Persons and noted that many people are still unaware of the various schemes and Acts available to them. He delivered an insightful address on the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, emphasizing the importance of senior citizens being informed about such provisions.

 

He further emphasized that awareness is crucial, stressing that every senior citizen should be informed about the various Acts and welfare schemes designed to support them. He also advised that individuals should refrain from distributing their land or property to their children while they are still alive, as it can often lead to complications.

 

Additionally, he noted that social welfare inspectors should work closely with the Panchayats to ensure that senior citizens are made aware of the schemes and benefits available to them. Strengthening this collaboration would help older persons access the support they need more effectively.

 

The programme also included a segment in which three senior citizens were presented with letters of felicitation. As a gesture of appreciation blankets, walking sticks, wheelchairs, hearing aids, knee braces, and hip braces were distributed to elderly attendees. This was followed by the honouring of retired employees and senior community members for their service and contributions to society.

 

The programme also featured cultural presentations and musical performances by senior citizens as well as participating officials. The programme had the presence of panchayat members, senior citizens, staff from WCSC&D welfare department and staff from Melli Dara GPU. The programme concluded with all attendees coming together to sing Sikkim’s State Anthem, “Jaha Bagcha Teesta Rangit”.

title: Changing Perspectives on Ageing– Best Practices in So
location: Event, Khajamalai Campus, Tiruchirappalli, Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu
descriptionHtml:
Ageing is a natural process encompassing physical, psychological, and social changes over time. With the global population of people aged 65 and older expected to more than double from 761 million in 2021 to 1.6 billion by 2050 (World Social Report 2023- UNDESA), addressing the myriad problems faced by the elderly, such as health issues, social isolation, and financial insecurity, is essential. This irreversible trend, driven by demographic transitions toward longer lives and smaller families, is occurring even in youthful countries. By 2050, 1 in 6 people globally will be 65 or older, up from 1 in 10 in 2021 (World Social Report 2023- UNDESA). As fertility rates fall, the proportion of younger people declines, while the shares of working-age adults and older individuals increase, driven by longer, healthier lifespans. Healthy ageing emphasizes maintaining physical, mental, and social well-being as people grow older, enhancing their quality of life. Social work, particularly gerontological social work, plays a crucial role in supporting the elderly. Our symposium will explore these aspects, showcasing best practices to promote healthy and dignified ageing.

  1. The Importance of Digital Literacy for Elderly People
  2. Caregiving for Older Adults with Chronic Neurological Conditions
  3. End-of-Life Care
  4. Research on Elderly – The Way Ahead
  5. The Need for Gerontological Social Work in Indian Academics
  6. Policies & Programmes for Elderly with Disabilities
  7. Intergenerational Bonding
  8. Feminism and Ageing
  9. Mental Health Problems of Older Persons
  10. Ageing Gracefully – The Role of CSR
  11. Social Gerontology
  12. Social Support Networks of Older People – Implications for Mental Health
  13. Empowering Our Elders – Reflections & Future Directions
  14. Creating Elderly-Friendly Environments

title: Digital & Financial Literacy ( Programme for Sr. Citize
location: Chintan Bhawan, Gangtok East Sikkim, Gangtok, Sikkim
descriptionHtml:
A one day programme for Senior Citizen on Digital & Financial Literacy under Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) organized by Women, Child, Senior Citizen & Divjangjan Welfare Department  at Chintan Bhawan on 27.01.2026.

The programme was attended by Ms. Manisha Cintury, Joint Secretary, Ms. Jyothsna Khatiwara, Assistant Director & Ms. Mani Kala Gurung, Social Welfare Officer. 
Mr. Thinley Zangpo Bhutia, Programmer, Cyber Crime CID Cell & Ms. Aditi Halder , Assistant Manager ,Reserve Bank of India,Gangtok were the resource person who spoke about Digital & Financial literacy and how cyber crime happens day in and day out at our State. 
The programme had the presence of Councillors, Senior Citizen Foundation of Sikkim along with Sikkim Retired Employees Association. Also the programme was attended by Senior Citizens of Gangtok District. 
The programme concluded with interactive sessions.

title: Digital Literacy & Cyber Security
location: Ashraysthal Sabhagar Girhinda Sheikhpura, Sheikhpura, Bihar
descriptionHtml:
One Day Awareness and Sensitization Programme on Digital Literacy & Cyber Security

Total Participants : 50

Venue : Ashraysthal Sabhagar, Vill.-Girhinda, Dist.-Sheikhpura, Bihar

Digital Literacy and Cyber Security Awareness Programme at Sheikhpura, aimed at empowering older adults to navigate the digital world safely and confidently. The programme was graced by Sheikhpura Cyber Crime DSP Ms. Jyoti Kumari, who highlighted how cyber frauds increasingly target older adults and shared practical preventive measures. She also informed participants about the National Cyber Crime Helpline Number (1930) for reporting suspected cyber frauds. Additional insights on responsible mobile phone usage and cyber safety were shared by resource persons Mr. Ram Lakhan Bharati and Mr. Tarun Kumar, further enriching the session.

title: District level Senior Citizen Meet
location: Balod, Shivni, Heerapur, Chhattisgarh
descriptionHtml:
Training cum orientation on digital literacy and financial literacy to senior citizens along with the MWPSC Act . Programme aimed at improved understanding regarding safe banking practices, pension-related financial management, and prevention of financial exploitation. The programme further strengthened awareness regarding the collective role of families, communities, and institutions in ensuring dignity, care, and inclusion of senior citizens.

The programme contributed significantly towards improving awareness among participants regarding digital and financial literacy. The digital literacy sessions enhanced participants’ understanding of basic mobile phone operations, use of communication applications, and safe digital practices. Senior citizens became more aware about precautions related to cyber fraud, fake calls, suspicious links, and misuse of personal and financial information.

The financial literacy component improved understanding regarding safe banking practices, use of ATM cards and passbooks, pension-related financial management, and the importance of maintaining confidentiality of banking details. Participants were also sensitized regarding financial fraud and exploitation and were encouraged to adopt safe financial practices while undertaking banking and digital transactions.

title: DoSJE organizes 28th Coordination Committee Meeting to devise Ways and Means to curb Offences of Untouchability and Atrocities against SCs and STs
descriptionHtml:
Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment (SJ&E), Dr. Virendra Kumar, and Union Minister for Tribal Affairs (TA), Shri Jual Oram, co-chaired the 28th meeting of the Committee to devise ways and means to curb offences of Untouchability and Atrocities against SCs and STs, in New Delhi  on 23 May 2025. It was also graced by the presence of Union Ministers of State, Dr. Ramdas Athawale, Shri B.L. Verma and Shri Durga Das Uikey.

In the meeting, discussions were held regarding charge sheet filing rate in the courts, pendency of cases in courts, status of Exclusive Special courts, meeting of Vigilance and  Monitoring Committees, pending grievances on National Helpline against Atrocities and Action plan to do away with shortcomings in implementation of the PCR and PoA Acts etc. was reviewed. The Committee reaffirmed the resolution of the Government to provide dignity to all the vulnerable sections of the society.

Union Minister, Dr. Virendra Kumar, in his concluding remarks, emphasized upon regular conduct of State Level and District Level Vigilance and Monitoring Committee Meetings to review the implementation of the provisions of Act in their respective States and Districts. State Officers were asked to take measures in order to ensure the SC & ST Population are not exploited in their States. Further, he emphasized upon increase in establishment of Special Police Stations, to fix accountability and take action against erring officials as per the provisions of PoA Act in case of neglect of duty.

The meeting concluded with a commitment from all participants to work together to ensure that the intent and spirit of these crucial Acts are upheld and justice is delivered to the victims of caste-based discrimination and atrocities. It witnessed participation from various States Governments at the level of Additional Chief Secretaries, Secretaries, Principal Secretaries/Secretaries of the SC/ST Development/Welfare Department, Home Department and Senior Police officials of the States/UTs attended the meeting.

Background

A committee, under the Chairpersonship of Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment along with the members from Ministry of Home Affairs, Tribal Affairs, Law and Justice, National Commission for Scheduled Castes, National Commission for Scheduled Tribes and three non-official members (two amongst SCs and one amongst STs), was set up in the year 2006 on the recommendation of the Parliamentary Committee on the Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. It aims to devise ways and means to curb offences of atrocities and ensure effective administration of the Protection of Civil Rights (PCR) Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities){PoA} Act, 1989.

title: Empowering Senior Citizens on Digital Literacy
location: Durtlang Leitan, Aizawl, Mizoram, Aizawl, Mizoram, -796014
descriptionHtml:
Introduction

In observance of the International Day of Older Persons (IDOP) 2025, the Regional Resource and Training Centre (RRTC), Mission Foundation Movement (MFM), organized a One-Day Workshop on “Digital Literacy among Senior Citizens” on 1st October 2025 at MFM Hall, Durtlang Leitan, Aizawl, Mizoram. The programme aimed to enhance the digital knowledge and skills of senior citizens and promote their inclusion in an increasingly digital society.

Objectives

The workshop was organized with the following objectives:

  • To create awareness on the importance of digital literacy among senior citizens.
  • To familiarize participants with the use of smartphones and digital applications.
  • To promote safe and responsible use of digital technology.
  • To encourage senior citizens to access digital services independently, including healthcare, banking, and communication services.

Participants

The programme witnessed the participation of senior citizens from various localities in and around Aizawl, along with representatives from senior citizens’ associations, volunteers, and staff of Mission Foundation Movement.

Proceedings

The programme commenced with an inaugural session and welcome address delivered by the organizers. The significance of celebrating the International Day of Older Persons and the importance of digital inclusion for older persons were highlighted.

Technical sessions were conducted by resource persons with expertise in information technology and digital services. The sessions covered the following topics:

  • Introduction to Digital Literacy and its Importance for Senior Citizens.
  • Basic Smartphone Operations and Internet Usage.
  • Digital Communication through WhatsApp and Video Calls.
  • Online Banking and Digital Payment Systems.
  • Accessing Government Services and Health Information Online.
  • Cyber Safety, Fraud Prevention, and Responsible Use of Social Media.

Hands-on demonstrations and interactive discussions enabled participants to practice the use of smartphones and various digital applications. Participants actively engaged in the sessions and sought clarification on issues related to online transactions and cyber security.

Outcome

The workshop successfully enhanced awareness and confidence among senior citizens in using digital technologies. Participants gained practical knowledge on accessing digital services and recognized the importance of staying connected in the digital age. The programme also contributed to reducing the digital divide and promoting active and independent ageing.

Conclusion

The One-Day Workshop on Digital Literacy among Senior Citizens, organized by RRTC, Mission Foundation Movement, in celebration of the International Day of Older Persons 2025, was successfully conducted. The programme served as an important initiative in empowering older persons with essential digital skills and promoting their social inclusion and well-being. Participants expressed appreciation for the practical nature of the training and recommended that similar programmes be organized regularly to enable senior citizens to keep pace with technological advancements.

descriptionHtml:
Grand Parents and Children’s (Mela)

Janata Highschool Vishrantwadi-Vishrantwadi Senior Citizens Association

Day- Saturday Date. 20/12/2025 Report– Afternoon 4 to 6.30 p.m.

 

On 20/12/2025, an Grand Parents and Children’s Gathering was at Janata High School, Vishrantwadi. At 4:00 pm, the programme was inaugurated by lighting the ceremonial lamp and by offering a garland to the idol of Goddess Saraswati. On this occasion, the President of the Pune City Senior Citizens Association Mr. Dilip Pawar, a philanthropist businessman, Mr. Rajendraji Chandak, Mr. Chandrakant Bhattad, and Headmaster Mr. Vairagar Sir were present. After that, Mr. Pawar as well as Mr. Chandak guided the gathering. Officer Shri Jaywant Mantri explained the purpose of the program and made an introduction.

After that, various activities were conducted with great enthusiasm and joy on the green playground, such as Snakes and Ladders, Carrom, ring toss, rubber ball throwing, carrying a ball behind the back and covering a fixed distance without dropping it, walking a fixed distance while balancing cups on the head without letting them fall, musical chairs, storytelling, solo songs, and dance performances. Through this programme, a sense of love and bonding between two generations was created. The children took a pledge that when the time comes to take care of their parents and elders, they will not send them to old-age homes. After that, everyone participated in group dancing to music. At the end, snacks and tea were served to all. The programme concluded with a vote of thanks delivered by Headmaster Mr. Vairagar Sir.Top of Form

title: Health Camp
location: Spandan Senior Women's Circle, Samudrapur, Hinganghat, Wardha, Maharashtra, -442305
descriptionHtml:
Health Check-up Camp and Guidance Lectures

A Health Check-up Camp was jointly organized by the Senior Citizens’ Institution, Spandan Senior Women’s Circle, and Janseva Foundation at Samudrapur, Hinganghat. 159 senior citizens (men and women) benefited from the camp.

Specialist medical officers conducted check-ups for various conditions, including eye diseases, dental problems, ear, nose, and throat (ENT), blood pressure, diabetes, heart conditions, and bone fractures. Along with the check-ups, specialist officers provided guidance on various diseases and the necessary precautions and remedies.

Following the camp, a guidance lecture was organized on how to live a life of dignity in old age. Former Principal Dr. Hasham Shaikh and Shri Hanumant Desai provided guidance. Dr. Shaikh advised on how to live and behave in a changing family environment and how to conduct oneself in society. He guided the audience on how to adapt to the changing social circumstances and take care to minimize trouble for family members.

Shri Hanumant Desai, a financial advisor, guided the audience on how to remain financially independent after retirement, covering topics like health insurance, pensions, and various beneficial investment options for deposits.

Shri Jaywant Mantri, Program Officer, gave the introductory address, highlighting the importance of the topics. Shri Ramkrishna Khuje, President of the Senior Citizens’ Institution, Hinganghat, was present. 105 senior citizens attended the lecture.

title: Health Camp for Senior Citizens
location: Mission Veng, Aizawl, Mizoram, -796005
descriptionHtml:
Introduction

In observance of the International Day of Older Persons (IDOP) 2025, the Regional Resource and Training Centre (RRTC), Mission Foundation Movement (MFM), organized a Health Camp for Senior Citizens on 1st October 2025 at Durtlang Leitan, Aizawl, Mizoram. The programme was organized with the objective of promoting healthy ageing and ensuring that older persons receive essential health care services and awareness on age-related health issues.

Objectives

The health camp was conducted with the following objectives:

  • To provide basic health screening and medical consultation for senior citizens.
  • To create awareness on preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyles.
  • To facilitate early detection and management of common age-related diseases.
  • To encourage regular health check-ups and healthy ageing practices.

Participants

Senior citizens from different localities of Aizawl and nearby areas participated in the health camp. Representatives from senior citizens’ associations, volunteers, healthcare professionals, and staff of Mission Foundation Movement also attended the programme.

Activities Conducted

The camp commenced with a brief inaugural session highlighting the significance of the International Day of Older Persons and the importance of maintaining good health in old age.

A team of doctors, nurses, and healthcare professionals conducted various health screening services, including:

  • General medical examination and consultation.
  • Blood pressure and blood sugar testing.
  • Body weight and Body Mass Index (BMI) assessment.
  • Eye and vision screening.
  • Counselling on nutrition, physical activity, and healthy lifestyle practices.
  • Health education on common age-related conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, arthritis, and cardiovascular diseases.

Participants received individual consultations and were advised on appropriate treatment and follow-up care whenever necessary. Referral services were also provided for those requiring further medical attention.

Outcome

The health camp benefitted senior citizens by providing access to basic healthcare services and increasing awareness regarding preventive health measures. Participants appreciated the opportunity to undergo health screening and receive professional medical advice. The programme contributed to promoting healthy and active ageing and enhanced awareness regarding the importance of regular health check-ups.

Conclusion

The Health Camp for Senior Citizens organized by the Regional Resource and Training Centre (RRTC), Mission Foundation Movement (MFM), in celebration of the International Day of Older Persons (IDOP) 2025 was successfully conducted. The programme served as a meaningful initiative to promote the health and well-being of older persons and reinforced the commitment of RRTC, MFM towards ensuring dignity, care, and quality of life for senior citizens.

title: Health & Wellness for Senior Citizens
location: Nanduara Ragunathpur Purulia, Nanduara Bagdipara Pahargora Ragunathpur Purulia, Purulia, West Bengal
descriptionHtml:
ONE DAY AWARENESS PROGRAM ON HEALTH & WELLNESS FOR SENIOR CITIZENS

Venue: Vill: Nanduara, Ward No: 10, Bagdipara, Pahargora, P.O+P.S:-Ragunathpur, Purulia, West Bengal, Pin: 723133

Total no of Participants: 52

Purulia, often described as “God’s own drawing over nature,” is a picturesque district of West Bengal, blessed with hills, green forests rich in flora and fauna, cascading waterfalls and colourful flowers that naturally promote mental well-being. However, behind this natural beauty lies a harsh reality marked by widespread poverty, extreme climatic conditions and inadequate health infrastructure, all of which contribute to significant health challenges among the local population.

With the support of the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India and under the initiative of CMIG, a health camp was organised in a remote tribal village named Nanduara (Bagdi Para), Pahargora, Ward No. 10, P.S. Raghunathpur, situated at the foothills of the renowned Joychandi Pahar.

The expressions on the villagers’ faces reflected their daily struggle for survival. During interactions, the medical team enquired about their health status, food availability, dietary habits and daily lifestyle. Some of the younger residents shared that due to food scarcity, they sometimes depend on wild animals such as wild boar and porcupine for sustenance. The presence of wild dogs and foxes in and around the village further highlights the vulnerability and isolation of the area.

Our primary objective was to extend medical support and offer moments of relief and reassurance to the community. The medical team conducted health check-ups, provided necessary medicines and offered guidance on health and nutrition. Most villagers were found to be suffering from age-related and chronic conditions such as COPD, hypertension, low back pain, osteoarthritis, hearing impairment, insomnia, loss of appetite and vertigo. A notable concern observed was severe muscle degeneration, largely attributed to prolonged nutritional deficiency.

The team not only addressed immediate medical needs but also engaged with the villagers to understand their pressing requirements and challenges. In return for our efforts, we were rewarded with warm smiles and heartfelt gratitude from the community—small yet deeply meaningful moments of connection. They sincerely acknowledge and thank the Government of India and CMIG for their invaluable support in making this outreach programme possible and for enabling us to serve one of the most underserved populations in this remote region of Purulia.

title: Health & Wellness Programme  for Senior Citizens
location: Shibganj Sundarban, Shibganj Sundarban South 24 Parganas, South 24 Parganas, West Bengal
descriptionHtml:
One Day Awareness Program on Health & Wellness for Senior Citizens

Venue: 5P83 7F3  Shibganj Sundarban South 24 Parganas,Pin-743312

Total no of Participants: 197 Senior Citizens

Calcutta Metropolitan Institute of Gerontology (CMIG) in collaboration with the Champa Mahila Society of Sundarbans in South 24 Parganas district of West Bengal, organized health camp and wellness program in Shibganj. The main objective of this program was to reach out to marginalized senior citizens who have limited access to healthcare services. The program included the distribution of blankets, general health check-ups and medicine supplies where health facilities are hard to reach. The event was attended by local doctors, paramedical staffs, officials from the Champa Mahila Society and representatives from CMIG, Kolkata.

The Sundarbans, one of the most remote and geographically challenging regions of West Bengal, is characterized by scattered islands, difficult waterways and limited connectivity. The people living in these areas face severe challenges in accessing basic healthcare services due to the absence of nearby hospitals, health centers and regular availability of medicines. Most villagers depend on long and costly travel by boat to reach the nearest health facility, which is often not feasible, especially for elderly persons. In this context, CMIG was organized a health camp in a remote area of the Sundarbans with the objective of providing basic healthcare services and free medicines to the underserved population. The camp focused on addressing common health problems such as fever, respiratory infections, gastrointestinal disorders, skin diseases, joint pain and general weakness which are prevalent due to poor living conditions, saline water and lack of sanitation. Blankets were distributed to 197 marginalized senior citizens of the locality who are extremely needy and does not possess any warm clothes in this winter season.

Qualified medical professionals examined the patients, provided necessary medical advice and distributed free medicines as per individual health needs. The health camp received an overwhelming response from the local population, reflecting the urgent need for regular healthcare services in the Sundarbans. The initiative helped reduce immediate health risks and provided relief to people who otherwise have no access to medicines or medical consultation.Such outreach programs are crucial in bridging the healthcare gap in remote and marginalized areas like the Sundarbans and contribute significantly towards improving the overall health and well-being of the community.

One Day Awareness and Sensitization Programme on Holistic Health including Yoga, Meditation & Natural therapy/Ayurveda

Place : Bhatta village in Nawada district,Bihar

The programme was organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MSJE) in collaboration with the Calcutta Metropolitan Institute of Gerontology (CMIG–RRTC), under the leadership of its Director Dr. Indrani Chakravorty and Samagra Seva Kendra, Bihar, headed by its Secretary Mr. Cheddi Prasad.

The programme commenced at Bhatta village in Nawada district, with a session on Yoga and Physiotherapy aimed at enhancing physical health, flexibility and mobility among older adults. Following a brief orientation, Ms. Moumita Basu conducted a body-tapping session to promote body awareness and relaxation. This was followed by Mr. Manish Kumar, who demonstrated elder-friendly yoga postures that participants could easily practice at home. The session concluded with Ms. Swaha Mitra Basu guiding participants through breathing and relaxation exercises, leaving them refreshed, energised and motivated to adopt healthier daily routines.

title: IDOP 2025 – KPHB
location: International Day of Older Persons, Kanyakaparameswari Auditorium, Phase-III, KPHB, Hyderabad, Hyderabad, Telangana
descriptionHtml:
The Heritage Foundation RRTC organized a programme on the International Day of Older Persons at the Kanyakaparameswari Auditorium, Phase III, Kukatpally Housing Board (KPHB), Hyderabad, on December 22, 2025. The Chief Guest for the program was Shri Malladi Krishna Rao, Hon'ble MLA of the Kukatpally Constituency. Two corporators from the same constituency were also present. Other notable attendees included Dr. K. R. Gangadharan, Chairman of the Heritage Foundation, Dr. G. Nageswara Rao, Retd Principal Scientist, Acharya NG Ranga University, Mr. Gangi Reddy, President and Mr. Koteswara Rao, Secretary of KPHB Phase-III Senior Citizens Welfare Association, and P. Reddy K, Project Director, HF RRTC.

Over 500 senior citizens from KPHB and the surrounding areas participated in the event.

title: Intergenerational Bonding in School
location: Pinjrawan High School Pinjrawan Panchayat Arwal, Arwal, Bihar
descriptionHtml:
One Day Awareness and Sensitization Programme on Promoting Intergenerational Bonding in School

Total no of Students : 55

Venue: Pinjrawan High School, 5r98+Gwr, Pinjrawan Panchayat, Arwal, Bihar, Pin Code – 804423

Intergenerational Bonding was organised at Pinjrawan High School, Arwal. A total of 55 students actively participated in drawing and essay writing activities designed to deepen their understanding of the importance of meaningful relationships between younger and older generations.Throughout the session, Resource Person Mr. Akhilesh Kumar guided students to reflect on generational gaps within families and communities, encouraging empathy, communication, and mutual respect. Students expressed enthusiastic appreciation for the programme, noting that such initiatives help them better understand the emotional needs of senior citizens and improve relationships with elders at home and in their neighbourhoods.The creative platforms allowed students to express their perspectives freely, offering valuable insights into youth perceptions of ageing, caregiving and intergenerational connection.

The State Level function of the International Day of Older Persons on 1st October, 2025 at The Ridge, Shimla, where the Hon’ble Chief Minister was preside over the occasion and the following activities was conducted during the function:-

  • Walkathon/Cyclothon for Sr. Citizens & Youths from the Ridge, Shimla to the AG Chowk..

title: International Day of Older Person
location: Shri Saurashtra Leuva Patel Seva Samaj, Shri Saurashtra Leuva Patel Seva Samaj Sector 7 Gandhinagar, Gandhinagar, Gujarat
descriptionHtml: This event, organized by Elderline-Gujarat (C/o HelpAge India) in collaboration with the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment / Women and Child Development, Gujarat, took place on 1st October, 2025, at the Shri Saurashtra Leuva Patel Seva Samaj, Sector 7, Gandhinagar. Aligning with the core vision of the International Day of Older Persons (IDOP) to promote senior welfare, advocate for elder rights, and foster an inclusive society that honors aging with dignity, the gathering drew a total of 216 attendees, prominently including 177 senior citizens. The event brought together key institutional figures such as Shri H. M. Panchal (President, Senior Citizens Council, Gandhinagar), Shri Kishorbhai V. Sheladiya (President, Shri Saurashtra Leuva Patel Seva Samaj), and Shri Jitendrasinh Solanki from Samaj Suraksha, Gandhinagar. Shri Shankarsinh Gohil (Member, Gujarat Bar Council & President, Gandhinagar Bar Association) graced the occasion as the Chief Guest, while the insightful panel discussions featured Shri Avinash Raval (CSR) and Shri Pavan Jain (Chief Operating Officer, Yuva Unstoppable) to further the shared mission of empowering and protecting our elderly community.

descriptionHtml:
On the occasion of International Yoga Day, a one-day yoga camp was successfully organized at ‘Sahara’—an old-age home in West Champaran managed by the District Social Security Cell under the Bihar Government’s Social Welfare Department.

All the senior citizens residing at the home participated enthusiastically in the event and pledged to lead a healthy, disease-free life through regular yoga practice. Yoga Guru Dharmendra Sharma attended the camp as the instructor and guided the senior citizens in practicing various *asanas* (yoga postures) and *pranayama* (breathing exercises).

title: “Labanya”: Grace, Within and Around   Celebration o
location: Rotary Sadan Kolkata, 94/2, Chowringee Rd, Maidan, Kolkata, Kolkata, West Bengal
descriptionHtml:
“Labanya”: Grace, Within and Around 

 Celebration of IDOP Concluding Programme (Part – II)

Date : 15th May,2026

Total Number of Participants:132

 

Calcutta Metropolitan Institute of Gerontology, Regional Resource and Training Center on Ageing, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, presented a show called “ Labanya” on 15th May at Rotary Sadan. The show was brought to life by graceful dance performances of senior citizens showing age is just a number. Inspired by dance therapy concepts and choreographed by London based researcher Dr Esha Chakravarty, Labanya highlighted graceful and active ageing through Rabindrasangeet and other popular numbers. 

Adding a deeply inspiring dimension to the programme, cancer survivors shared their journeys- from the challenges of diagnosis to emerging as courageous fighters with renewed strength, while reflecting the therapeutic potential of dance. 

The senior citizens who graced the programme through meaningful movement, expression and storytelling were Susmita Chowdhuri, Mala Ghosh and her group, Sumanta Chattopadhyay, CMIG’s Day Care Center beneficiaries, Sunita Chandra alongwith CMIG students Kalyan Dey and Dr Udita Ghosh Sarkar and theatre group Swarashruti 

The programme was inaugurated by CMIG Director Dr Indrani Chakravarty and closed by CMIG President Sri Santi Ranjan Chakraborty. This was a rare and meaningful celebration where grace, healing and human spirit came together on one stage.
