descriptionHtml:
One Day Awareness and Sensitization Programme on Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizen Act 2007

Total Participants : 53

Venue: Satgama Village ,Jamui District in Bihar

An Awareness and Sensitization Programme on the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 was organised in Jamui district. Participants were informed about the objectives, key provisions and significance of the Act, along with details of the Elder Line Toll-Free Helpline Number (14567). The session witnessed active participation, with several questions raised regarding legal rights, grievance redressal and implementation mechanisms. Resource persons from CMIG–RRTC addressed these queries comprehensively, ensuring greater clarity and awareness among participants.

MoU signed between Department of Social Justice & Empowerment and National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) for Awareness Generation on Social Welfare Schemes
descriptionHtml:
The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE), Government of India, and the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 30/09/2024 in New Delhi. This significant partnership is aimed at enhancing public awareness about various Acts, Rules and Schemes of the Department, especially those designed to support the marginalized and vulnerable sections of society.

NALSA, constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act of 1987, has a mandate to provide legal aid to disadvantaged groups and spread legal literacy. Through this MoU, both NALSA and DoSJE will conduct a series of campaigns, seminars, and events to increase the reach and impact of social welfareschemes for vulnerable communities across India.

The MoU was signed in the presence of Shri Virendra Kumar, Union Minister for Social Justice & Empowerment, and Shri Justice Sanjiv Khanna, Judge of the Supreme Court of India & Executive Chairman of NALSA. The event also witnessed the official launch of the SARTHIE 1.0 initiative, a joint effort intended to empower disadvantaged communities, including Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Senior Citizens, Transgender Persons, Victims of Alcoholism and Substance Abuse, persons engaged in the act of Begging, Denotified and Nomadic Tribes, and more.

The SARTHIE 1.0 initiative also aligns with the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, particularly the goals focused on eradicating poverty, reducing inequality, and promoting social protection policies that ensure greater equality for all. The collaboration aims to bridge the awareness gap and provide legal assistance to ensure the effective implementation of social welfare programmes. The launch of SARTHIE 1.0 during this event marks a crucial step toward addressing the needs of the most vulnerable sections of society through awareness generation and legal support, empowering them to access government welfare schemes more effectively. The synergy between the DoSJE and NALSA will ensure that the social justice to all is further strengthened.

In collaboration with NALSA, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment will ensure that awareness generation and outreach extends to the grassroot level. Under this partnership, State Legal Services Authorities (SLSAs) and District Legal Services Authorities (DLSAs), will organize awareness camps across the country through the para-legal volunteers and panel lawyers. The camps will focus on ensuring awareness of the five important Acts being implemented by the Department:

1. Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955

2. Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989

3. The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007

4. The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019

5. Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013

Besides ensuring outreach of the various schemes of the department, these legal awareness and outreach initiatives will range from Panchayat to State level, ensuring that the targeted audiences are made aware of their legal rights and the government welfare programmes available to them.

title: Observance of World Elder Abuse Awareness Day Walkathon
location: CMIG premises to Jamuna Nagar, Jamuna Nagar, Kolkata 99, Kolkata, West Bengal
descriptionHtml:
The Calcutta Metropolitan Institute of Gerontology (CMIG) is supported by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MSJE), Govt of India. As per National Mandate, CMIG has been encouraged to observe ‘WEAAD’ on 15th June,2026. 

CMIG organised a ‘Walkathon’ to promote respect, inclusion and care for senior citizens. A wide scale participation in the event included participants from senior citizens, community members, health care professionals among other pertinent stakeholders. Elder abuse encompasses physical, emotional, financial components which remain severely underreported. WHO has recognised 1 in 24 elder abuse cases which have been documented throughout several years. According to United Nation General Assembly (UNGA), World Elder Abuse Awareness Day (WEAAD) serves as a call to action in order to protect the rights, safety and dignity of the elderly. CMIG has identified social isolation as one of the major risk factors for elderly abuse.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Indrani Chakravarty, Director of CMIG stated- “Elder abuse often remains hidden and underreported due to fear of retaliation and stigmatization. Through this Walkathon, we aim to raise public awareness and inspire collective responsibility to ensure that older persons live with dignity, respect, and protection. A society that values and cares for its elders is a stronger and more compassionate society. Moreover, we are involving our Day Care beneficiaries to be the part of the Walkathon”.

CMIG invited citizens, institutions, and community leaders to join hands in recognizing the contributions of older persons and fostering an environment where they can live free from abuse, neglect, and discrimination.

descriptionHtml:
One Day Awareness and Sensitization Programme On Promoting Intergenerational Bonding In School

Date : 9th December,2025

Total no of Students: 60

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MSJ&E), together with the Calcutta Metropolitan Institute of Gerontology (CMIG) under the leadership of Director Dr. Indrani Chakravorty and Samagra Seva Kendra, Bihar, headed by Secretary Cheddi Peasad, conducted a series of programmes focused on enhancing the wellbeing of senior citizens and fostering stronger intergenerational bonds.Awareness and Sensitization programme on promoting intergenerational bonding in school was organised  at National Town Inter School, Aurangabad district in Bihar. 60 students engaged in drawing and essay competitions that highlighted their perspectives on empathy and mutual respect between generations. Cash prizes were awarded to the top three entries in each category. The programme was supported by school representatives Santosh Kumar and Dayananda Kumar in their role as a resource person. Many highlighted that such programmes help them understand the emotional needs of senior citizens, promote compassion and improve communication with elders at home and in their neighbourhoods. The creative platforms of drawing and essay competitions allowed students to express their feelings freely, offering meaningful insights into how young people perceive ageing, caregiving and intergenerational connection.

title: One Day Awareness on Healing through science and moveme
location: Purbalok EM Bypass Kalikapur, 43 Purbalok EM Bypass Kalikapur Kolkata, Kolkata, West Bengal
descriptionHtml:
One Day Awareness on Healing through science and movement new roads in cancer care and ageing

Date: 20thDecember, 2025

Venue: 43 Purbalok EM Bypass Kalikapur Kolkata-700099

Dr. Esha Chakravarty (MSc Microbiology, MSc Cancer Biology, PhD Cancer Biology) has specialised in targeted cancer therapy since 2013. In the early stages of her career in the UK, she began developing novel therapeutic strategies for cancer and later undertook extensive research focused on designing new antibodies for ovarian cancer, with particular emphasis on identifying diagnostic and therapeutic targets. Her work resulted in publications in reputable high-impact journals, including Frontiers in Immunology.

Alongside mainstream therapeutic research, Dr. Chakravarty initiated an independent project exploring the potential of dance therapy in age-care and terminal illnesses such as cancer, in collaboration with CMIG. This work was presented under the Health Sciences category at the Gerontological Society of America.

In her lecture-cum-workshop held on 20 December, she addressed key aspects of geriatric oncology, generating awareness on why cancer in older adults require special clinical, psychosocial, and supportive care approaches. The session highlighted the unique challenges faced by elderly cancer patients, including frailty, co-morbidities, reduced treatment tolerance, and quality-of-life considerations, underscoring the need for holistic and patient-centred care models.

The workshop emphasised the crucial role of supportive therapies such as dance psychotherapy in cancer rehabilitation, recovery, and emotional well-being. Particular focus was given to how movement-based interventions can support physical confidence, emotional expression, and stress management, not only for patients but also for caregivers who often experience significant psychological and emotional burden.

The session was attended by caregivers, nurses, teaching professionals, and other medical and allied healthcare professionals. It provided an interactive platform for sharing real-life experiences from cancer survivors and caregivers, and received valuable input from medical professionals, enriching the discussion through multidisciplinary perspectives. The workshop also laid the foundation for follow-up initiatives and will be continued through further structured and practical programmes aimed at sustained engagement and impact in geriatric oncology care.

location: PX97RH3 Monohar Bahal B Asansol Paschim Bardhaman West Bengal, Paschim Bardhaman, West Bengal, -713341
descriptionHtml:
A Pilgrimage to the limitless Horizon : Approaching Totality

 

Date: 9th December,2025

At the wee hours of dawn when the troubled soul feels serene by the loving warmth of the morning shine, we set out for a ‘One Day Awareness and Sensitization Programme on Health & Wellness Programme’scheduled to be held on that very day in the outskirts of Asansol, Paschim Bardhaman. We perceived and comprehended an entirely new dynamics amongst Senior Citizens of the place. We saw familial bonding, unconditional love and respect which time & social/ demographic changes haven’t been able to turnish. What they locked was an organized infrastructure exclusively for Senior Citizens with younger candidates who have no formal training in Geriatric Caregiving despite having the purest of bonding with members of the Silver Age Cohort.

We proposed a model which when implemented and executed in real-time, will eventually lead towards the genesis of eSHG with a small initial capital and financial empowerment, health equity, community resilience as well as Human Rights Advocacy. This abides by and enshrines the entire spectrum of our activities directed towards fulfillment of UN IDOP 2025 Central Theme.

We are now sculpting a firm pedestal upon which generic and tailor-made interventions could be implemented with the sole intention of composing on algorithmic blueprint with an Impact Matrix which will catalyze ‘Healthy Ageing’ as defined by WHO. We have already set sail on this mission with unwavering faith on the grace of the Almighty and generous help and active guidance from the Central Governance.

.

Saludos Cordiales

We salute thee

title: One Day Awareness Programme on Health  Wellness for Sen
location: Bankura Gangajalghati Bisinda Bankura, Bankura, Gangajalghati - Block(Gram), Bisinda, Bankura, Bankura, West Bengal
descriptionHtml:
AURA OF GOLD & SILVER: 

A synopsis of Health & Wellness Camp in Bankura, Gangajalghati – Block(Gram), Bisinda, Bankura, West Bengal,722133.

 

“He who has “WHY” to live can bear almost any “HOW”.

 

CMIG conducted a Health & Wellness Camp in the remote area of Gangajalghati, Block(Gram), Bisinda, Bankura, West Bengal,722133.

 

The mission was unique in the sense that never before a Health Camp of this nature has been conducted amidst the tribal population of the district. Apart from routine Medical Camp activities, we unearthed a new ‘mode’ of maintaining well-being amongst the Senior Citizens of the tribal populace.

 

Crescent Formation: 8 females standing hand-in-hand flanked by 4 (2+2) male drummers formed a ‘Crescent” Like standing orientation The drums started beating slowly yet rhythmically synergized with the local tribal song. The ‘Crescent ‘group initiated a slow dance with a rhythm that felt subline, reflective of the serene gleam of the ‘Silver moon’. This form of entertainment was something, seemed almost effortless and yet it served to increase body balance, unified rhythm, solace of the heart as well as strengthening the core soft twitch muscles which are the prime movers of enhanced stance posture control and stability of gait. Detailed feedback was taken from each & every participant of this mega event.

 

Percentage distribution of major health issues of the area was documented which will be included as a pie chart in main report which will facilitate detailed understanding of necessary and pertinent interventions to promote Healthy Ageing a defined by WHO amongst the Senior Citizens of the tribal fraternity.

descriptionHtml:
One Day Awareness Programme on Health & Wellness for Senior Citizen – BIHAR

Venue: Meeting Hall, Samagra Seva kendra, P O – Barachatti, Dist.- Gaya G(Bihar), Pin code – 824201

Total no of participants: 56

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MSJE), together with the Calcutta Metropolitan Institute of Gerontology (CMIG) under the leadership of Director Dr. Indrani Chakravorty and Samagra Seva Kendra, Bihar, headed by Secretary Cheddi Peasad, conducted a series of programmes focused on enhancing the wellbeing of senior citizens and fostering stronger intergenerational bonds. One Day Awareness Programme on Health & Wellness for Senior Citizen was conducted with a comprehensive health camp at Kendua village, Barachatti, Bihar where elderly participants received essential health check-ups and medical consultations. Based on their individual diagnoses and requirements, necessary medicines were distributed, including Telvas 40 for blood pressure management, Bigonet 500 for diabetes care, A–Z multivitamin tablets for strengthening overall health, Deltanac-P for pain and inflammation relief, Clavan 625 as an antibiotic for infection control, and Calpol 500 for fever and mild pain. Rakesh Singh, Health Manager of Barachatti CHC, graced the occasion and extended his support to this community welfare initiative. Many older adults expressed their satisfaction, sharing that the doctor’s attentive approach and the time dedicated to understanding their health concerns made them feel truly heard and cared for.

title: One Day Programme for staff of NGOs, senior citizen hom
location: Living Home Hall, Nabam Deepak Living Home Hall, Itanagar, Papum Pare, Arunachal Pradesh
descriptionHtml:
A One Day Programme for Staff of NGOs and Senior Citizen Homes focusing on PFMS, documentation, e-Anudaan, proposal development, resource augmentation, fund raising, and institutional linkages was successfully conducted on 16 March 2026 at Nabam Deepak Living Home Hall, Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh. The programme was organised with the objective of strengthening the administrative, financial, and project management capacities of NGO personnel working in the field of elderly care and social welfare.

The programme began with a brief inaugural session in which the organizers highlighted the growing need for professional management practices in NGOs and senior care institutions. Emphasis was laid on transparency, proper financial management, and sustainable resource mobilization to ensure effective service delivery to senior citizens and other vulnerable groups.

 

Technical Sessions 

A series of informative sessions were conducted by experienced resource persons covering key thematic areas:

  • Public Financial Management System (PFMS):
    Participants were introduced to the importance of PFMS in ensuring transparency and accountability in utilization of government grants. Demonstrations were given on registration, fund tracking, and reporting procedures.
  • Documentation and Record Management:
    The session focused on maintaining proper records, preparing utilization certificates, and systematic filing practices essential for audits and organizational credibility.
  • e-Anudaan Portal:
    Resource persons provided practical guidance on online submission of grant applications, updating organizational profiles, and tracking proposal status through the e-Anudaan system.
  • Proposal Development:
    Participants were trained on preparing effective project proposals, including problem analysis, logical framework, budgeting, and outcome indicators. The importance of aligning proposals with donor priorities was also discussed.
  • Resource Augmentation and Fund Raising:
    Strategies for mobilizing funds from government agencies, corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives, and community contributions were shared. Participants were encouraged to adopt innovative approaches such as networking, partnership building, and digital fund-raising platforms.
  • Institutional Linkages:
    The session highlighted the significance of establishing linkages with government departments, health institutions, local bodies, and community organizations to enhance service outreach and programme sustainability.

Participation and Interaction 

The programme witnessed active participation from staff members of various NGOs and senior citizen homes. Interactive discussions, practical demonstrations, and experience-sharing sessions enabled participants to clarify doubts and gain hands-on understanding of the topics covered.

 

Conclusion 

The one-day programme concluded with a feedback session where participants expressed appreciation for the practical relevance of the training. The organizers reiterated the importance of continuous capacity building and collaboration to improve the quality of services provided to senior citizens.

Overall, the programme proved to be informative and beneficial, enhancing the knowledge and skills of NGO personnel in financial management, project planning, and resource mobilization, thereby contributing to stronger and more sustainable social welfare initiatives.

Title of the Programme: One Day Programme on Standardization of Senior Care Homes and Management
Date: 23rd February 2026
Venue: Jowai, West Jaintia Hills, Meghalaya
 

Introduction

A One Day Programme on Standardization of Senior Care Homes and Management was successfully conducted on 23rd February 2026 at Jowai, West Jaintia Hills, Meghalaya. The programme was organized with the objective of promoting quality standards and improving management systems in senior care homes. The initiative focused on strengthening institutional care services and ensuring dignified living conditions for senior citizens.

 

Objectives of the Programme

  • To create awareness on minimum standards for senior care homes
  • To improve management and administrative practices
  • To enhance caregiving skills of staff and volunteers
  • To promote proper documentation and record keeping
  • To emphasize health, hygiene, and safety of senior citizens

Proceedings of the Programme

The programme commenced with a welcome address highlighting the importance of standardization in senior care homes. The introductory session emphasized the growing need for structured care systems due to the increasing elderly population. Participants were informed about the importance of adopting uniform operational guidelines to ensure quality services.

The technical sessions covered various aspects of senior care home management. Discussions were held on infrastructure requirements, sanitation, nutrition, and healthcare support for residents. Resource persons also explained the importance of maintaining records such as admission registers, medical records, and daily activity logs.

Special emphasis was given to psychosocial care and emotional well-being of senior citizens. Participants were encouraged to conduct recreational activities, counselling sessions, and community interaction programmes to reduce loneliness and isolation among elderly residents.

Safety and security measures in senior care homes were also discussed, including emergency preparedness, fall prevention, and regular health monitoring. The importance of trained caregivers and capacity building programmes for staff members was highlighted during the session.

 

Participation

The programme was attended by functionaries of senior citizen homes, social workers, community leaders, volunteers, and individuals involved in elderly care services. Participants actively took part in discussions and shared their experiences and challenges. The interactive nature of the programme helped in clarifying doubts and exchanging practical solutions.

 

Outcome of the Programme

  • Increased awareness on standardization of senior care homes
  • Improved knowledge on management and caregiving practices
  • Better understanding of health and psychosocial needs of elderly residents
  • Strengthened coordination among stakeholders
  • Encouragement to adopt proper documentation and monitoring systems

Conclusion

The programme concluded with a summary of the key issues discussed and recommendations for improving the quality of services in senior care homes. Participants expressed their appreciation for the informative sessions and showed willingness to implement the suggested standards. The One Day Programme is expected to contribute towards strengthening the management and standardization of senior care homes in West Jaintia Hills, Meghalaya.

descriptionHtml:
A one-day workshop on elderly issues was successfully organized at Itanagar by the Regional Resource Training Centre (RRTC) for Senior Citizens, Mission Foundation Movement. The programme was designed to address the multifaceted challenges faced by senior citizens and to promote a supportive and inclusive environment for the ageing population.

Objectives

The primary objectives of the workshop were to create a platform for discussing the social, psychological, and health-related challenges encountered by elderly persons. The programme also aimed to promote community-based care systems that encourage family and societal involvement in elderly welfare. Additionally, emphasis was placed on strengthening intergenerational bonding, fostering mutual respect and understanding between younger and older generations. Another key objective was to encourage active ageing and enhance mental well-being among senior citizens through awareness, participation, and engagement in meaningful activities.

Participants

The workshop witnessed the participation of around 30 individuals, including senior citizens, organizational staff, volunteers, and representatives from various non-governmental organizations. The diverse composition of participants contributed to a rich exchange of ideas, experiences, and perspectives on elderly care and support systems.

Outcomes

The workshop resulted in several positive outcomes. There was a noticeable improvement in awareness regarding the rights of senior citizens and the various welfare provisions available for them. Participants, especially youth and volunteers, demonstrated a strengthened commitment to supporting the elderly in their communities. The programme also facilitated the identification of potential areas for collaboration between NGOs and government departments, paving the way for more coordinated and effective service delivery. Furthermore, the elderly participants were encouraged to remain socially active, maintain a positive outlook, and actively engage in community life, thereby improving their overall well-being.

Conclusion

In conclusion, the workshop proved to be an effective initiative in raising awareness about issues concerning senior citizens. It fostered mutual understanding and respect between generations and highlighted the collective responsibility of society to care for and support the elderly. The programme reinforced the importance of continued efforts toward building an age-friendly community where senior citizens are valued, respected, and empowered.

title: One Day Workshop on Elderly Issues
location: Vaivakawn, Aizawl, Aizawl, Mizoram, -796009
descriptionHtml:
A one-day workshop on elderly issues was successfully organized by the Regional Resource and Training Centre (RRTC) at the Vaivakawn Cultural Centre-cum-Auditorium, Aizawl. The programme aimed to create awareness, enhance knowledge, and promote the well-being of senior citizens by addressing key aspects of ageing, including health, rights, and active living. A total of 170 senior citizen members from different localities of Aizawl West actively participated in the workshop, reflecting strong community engagement and interest in the welfare of older persons.

 

The programme was chaired by Ms. Esther Lalthachawii, Project Manager, who guided the proceedings and ensured the smooth conduct of the event. The introductory address was delivered by Mr. K. Lalnghinglova, Board Member of Mission Foundation Movement, who highlighted the importance of such initiatives in empowering senior citizens and improving their quality of life. He emphasized the organization’s commitment to supporting older persons through awareness programmes, capacity building, and access to essential services.

 

The technical sessions covered a wide range of topics relevant to the ageing population. Ms. Lalremtluangi, Tutor at MFM School of Nursing, delivered an informative session on common diseases among the elderly, including hypertension, diabetes, arthritis, and other age-related conditions. She also discussed preventive measures, early detection, and available treatment options, encouraging participants to adopt healthy lifestyles and seek timely medical care.

 

Mr. Lalremsiama, Fitness Trainer, conducted a session on physical exercise, emphasizing the importance of maintaining regular physical activity even in old age. He demonstrated simple and safe exercises suitable for senior citizens and provided practical guidance on exercises that could be performed at home without the need for special equipment, thereby promoting independence and physical well-being.

Mr. Lalbiaksanga, Team Leader of the National Helpline for Senior Citizens, delivered a session on the rights and entitlements of older persons. He elaborated on various government schemes, legal safeguards, and support mechanisms available to senior citizens, and encouraged them to be aware of their rights and to seek assistance whenever required.

 

Further enriching the programme, Mr. K.D. Lalthiamsama, Lecturer at Laithangpuii College of Pharmacy, spoke on the rational use of medicines among senior citizens. He highlighted the importance of adhering to prescribed medications, understanding correct dosages, and avoiding self-medication, particularly among older adults with multiple health conditions.

 

The workshop concluded with a valedictory address by Mr. R. Vanlalzauva, Director of Mission Foundation Movement. In his remarks, he expressed appreciation for the enthusiastic participation of the senior citizens and the valuable contributions of the resource persons. He reaffirmed the organization’s commitment to promoting the dignity, health, and overall well-being of older persons and called for continued collaboration among stakeholders to ensure a supportive and age-friendly environment for senior citizens in the community.

 

Overall, the workshop proved to be highly beneficial in enhancing awareness and empowering senior citizens with knowledge and practical information essential for healthy and active ageing.

The workshop witnessed the participation of around 30 individuals, including senior citizens, organizational staff, volunteers, and representatives from various non-governmental organizations. The diverse composition of participants contributed to a rich exchange of ideas, experiences, and perspectives on elderly care and support systems.

Outcomes

The workshop resulted in several positive outcomes. There was a noticeable improvement in awareness regarding the rights of senior citizens and the various welfare provisions available for them. Participants, especially youth and volunteers, demonstrated a strengthened commitment to supporting the elderly in their communities. The programme also facilitated the identification of potential areas for collaboration between NGOs and government departments, paving the way for more coordinated and effective service delivery. Furthermore, the elderly participants were encouraged to remain socially active, maintain a positive outlook, and actively engage in community life, thereby improving their overall well-being.

Conclusion

In conclusion, the workshop proved to be an effective initiative in raising awareness about issues concerning senior citizens. It fostered mutual understanding and respect between generations and highlighted the collective responsibility of society to care for and support the elderly. The programme reinforced the importance of continued efforts toward building an age-friendly community where senior citizens are valued, respected, and empowered.

title: One Day Workshop on Elderly Issues
location: Vaivakawn cultural centre cum auditorium, Vaivakawn, Aizawl, Aizawl, Mizoram
descriptionHtml:
A one-day workshop on elderly issues was successfully organized by the Regional Resource and Training Centre (RRTC) at the Vaivakawn Cultural Centre-cum-Auditorium, Aizawl. The programme aimed to create awareness, enhance knowledge, and promote the well-being of senior citizens by addressing key aspects of ageing, including health, rights, and active living. A total of 170 senior citizen members from different localities of Aizawl West actively participated in the workshop, reflecting strong community engagement and interest in the welfare of older persons.

 

The programme was chaired by Ms. Esther Lalthachawii, Project Manager, who guided the proceedings and ensured the smooth conduct of the event. The introductory address was delivered by Mr. K. Lalnghinglova, Board Member of Mission Foundation Movement, who highlighted the importance of such initiatives in empowering senior citizens and improving their quality of life. He emphasized the organization’s commitment to supporting older persons through awareness programmes, capacity building, and access to essential services.

 

The technical sessions covered a wide range of topics relevant to the ageing population. Ms. Lalremtluangi, Tutor at MFM School of Nursing, delivered an informative session on common diseases among the elderly, including hypertension, diabetes, arthritis, and other age-related conditions. She also discussed preventive measures, early detection, and available treatment options, encouraging participants to adopt healthy lifestyles and seek timely medical care.

 

Mr. Lalremsiama, Fitness Trainer, conducted a session on physical exercise, emphasizing the importance of maintaining regular physical activity even in old age. He demonstrated simple and safe exercises suitable for senior citizens and provided practical guidance on exercises that could be performed at home without the need for special equipment, thereby promoting independence and physical well-being.

Mr. Lalbiaksanga, Team Leader of the National Helpline for Senior Citizens, delivered a session on the rights and entitlements of older persons. He elaborated on various government schemes, legal safeguards, and support mechanisms available to senior citizens, and encouraged them to be aware of their rights and to seek assistance whenever required.

 

Further enriching the programme, Mr. K.D. Lalthiamsama, Lecturer at Laithangpuii College of Pharmacy, spoke on the rational use of medicines among senior citizens. He highlighted the importance of adhering to prescribed medications, understanding correct dosages, and avoiding self-medication, particularly among older adults with multiple health conditions.

 

The workshop concluded with a valedictory address by Mr. R. Vanlalzauva, Director of Mission Foundation Movement. In his remarks, he expressed appreciation for the enthusiastic participation of the senior citizens and the valuable contributions of the resource persons. He reaffirmed the organization’s commitment to promoting the dignity, health, and overall well-being of older persons and called for continued collaboration among stakeholders to ensure a supportive and age-friendly environment for senior citizens in the community.

 

Overall, the workshop proved to be highly beneficial in enhancing awareness and empowering senior citizens with knowledge and practical information essential for healthy and active ageing.

title: Pilgrimage tour of beneficiaries of all 03 Old Age Home
location: Ravangla Pelling Namchi, Namchi, Sikkim
descriptionHtml:
A three-day pilgrimage tour for the beneficiaries of the old age homes of Boomtar Namchi, Ranipool, and Tintek Lee All Sangh was successfully organised by the Women, Child, Senior Citizen and Divyangjan Welfare Department from 31st January 2026 to 2nd February 2026 within Sikkim. The tour was arranged with the noble objective of providing spiritual enrichment, recreation, and emotional well-being to the senior citizens while also encouraging social bonding and cultural exposure. The tour was led by Ms. Jyotshna Khatiwara, Assistant Director of the department, and was accompanied by departmental officials Mr. Pem Tshering Lepcha and Mr. Gaurav Pradhan, who ensured the smooth coordination and successful conduct of the programme throughout the journey.

 

On the first day, 31st January 2026, the group travelled to Pelling via Ravangla, enjoying the scenic beauty, serene surroundings, and peaceful atmosphere along the route. The elderly beneficiaries were delighted by the pleasant climate and breathtaking views of the hills and valleys, making the journey both refreshing and memorable.

 

On the second day, 1st February 2026, the beneficiaries visited the famous Chenrezig Sky Walk and the sacred Khecheopalri Lake. The spiritual ambience of the holy lake and the magnificent experience of the Sky Walk filled the participants with joy, peace, and devotion. The visit provided an opportunity for the senior citizens to spend meaningful time together while appreciating the rich cultural and spiritual heritage of Sikkim.

 

On the final day, 2nd February 2026, the group visited the revered Siddhesvara Dham (Char Dham) at Namchi. The pilgrims offered prayers and sought blessings for peace, good health, and prosperity. The tour concluded successfully with happy memories, strengthened friendships, and a sense of spiritual fulfilment among all the participants.

The department’s thoughtful initiative was highly appreciated by the beneficiaries, as it brought happiness, comfort, and a refreshing change to their daily lives. Such programmes play a significant role in promoting the dignity, care, and well-being of senior citizens while fostering compassion, unity, and community spirit in society.

location: Gogunda Udaipur, Udaipur, Rajasthan
descriptionHtml:
A large-scale assistive device distribution camp was organized in Gogunda, Udaipur district, under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY). Camp was conducted by the Department of Social Justice and empowerment  in collaboration with ALIMCO (Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India).

Key Highlights

  • 974 senior citizens received assistive devices.
  • A total of 5,421 assistive aids were distributed.
  • The estimated value of the distributed equipment was approximately ₹80 lakh.
  • The initiative aims to improve the quality of life, mobility, and independence of elderly persons belonging to economically weaker sections.
  • Chief Guest Avinash Gehlot Sir, Hon’ble Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, stated that the government’s priority is to ensure that welfare schemes reach the last person in society.

Devices Distributed

The distribution included:

  • 152 wheelchairs
  • 341 commodes
  • 800 walking sticks
  • 147 rollators/walkers
  • 565 hearing aids
  • 262 silicone cushions
  • 825 spectacle sets
  • 420 walking support devices
  • Other assistive aids, taking the total to 5,421 devices.

title: Senior and Youth Connect Programme
location: Chief Minister Rehabilitation Home Sawaimadhopur, Sawai Madhopur, Rajasthan
descriptionHtml:
On 15 June, under the Seniors and Youth Connect Programme commemorating World Elder Abuse Awareness Day,  awareness and interaction programme was successfully organized at the Chief Minister Rehabilitation Home, Sawai Madhopur.

During the programme, youth participants interacted with elderly residents, and awareness was imparted regarding the prevention of elder abuse, cyber safety, legal rights of senior citizens, helpline services, and the importance of respectful treatment of elderly persons.

A total of 50 participants benefited from the programme. The activity contributed to enhancing awareness among youth regarding the challenges faced by senior citizens and the legal and social protection mechanisms available for their welfare.

title: Senior and Youth Connect Programme
location: Old age Home rajsamand, Meera Vidhya Prachar Sansthan Mohi Rajsamand, Rajsamand, Rajasthan
descriptionHtml:
On 15th and 16th June, under the Seniors and Youth Connect Programme commemorating World Elder Abuse Awareness Day, awareness, interaction, and environmental activities were successfully organized at the Old Age Home, Rajsamand.

During the programme, youth participants actively interacted with elderly residents and participated in awareness sessions on the prevention of elder abuse, cyber safety, legal rights of senior citizens, available helpline services, and the importance of treating elderly persons with dignity and respect. The programme also provided an opportunity for meaningful intergenerational engagement, fostering empathy and understanding among the youth.

In addition, a tree plantation drive was conducted within the premises, in which youth volunteers and elderly residents jointly participated. The activity promoted environmental awareness, community participation, and a sense of shared responsibility towards nature.

A total of 23 participants benefited from the programme. The activities contributed to enhancing awareness among youth regarding the challenges faced by senior citizens, the welfare and protection mechanisms available for them, and the importance of environmental conservation and community service.

title: Senior Citizens Association Meeting
location: Dhanvantri Bhawan, 1/3 Kayaji plot, Dhanvantri Bhawan, sada road morbi, Morbi, Gujarat
descriptionHtml:
Elderline Gujarat Awareness Programme – Senior Citizens Group Morbi

Elderline Gujarat, in collaboration with the Senior Citizens Association (SCA), Morbi, successfully organized an awareness programme on 3rd August 2026 at Dhanvantri Bhawan, Morbi.

The programme aimed to create awareness among senior citizens about their rights, welfare measures, and the support services available to them. During the session, participants were provided detailed information on 10 important government schemes designed for the welfare and empowerment of senior citizens. The benefits, eligibility criteria, and application process for each scheme were explained to help participants access these services effectively.

A special session was conducted on the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, highlighting its importance in protecting the rights and dignity of senior citizens. The discussion covered the legal provisions available under the Act, the responsibility of children and relatives towards elderly parents, and the remedies available for senior citizens seeking maintenance and support.

The interactive session encouraged participants to raise their queries, which were addressed by the resource persons. The programme concluded with a vote of thanks, reinforcing Elderline Gujarat’s commitment to ensuring that every senior citizen is informed about their rights and has access to the necessary support and assistance through the Elder Helpline 14567.

title: Sensitization and Awareness, Intergenerational Bonding
location: Mangan Community Hall Dzongu Kabi Tingda Lachen, Mangan District, Mangan, Sikkim
descriptionHtml:
Date: 06th Feb 2026

 The Women, Child, Senior Citizen & Divyangjan Development Department, Mangan, successfully organised an Awareness-cum-Walkathon programme for senior citizens of Mangan District under the Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVAY). The programme commenced with a walkathon from the DAC premises to the Community Hall, Mangan, followed by an awareness session. The initiative aimed to promote active ageing, enhance health awareness, and disseminate information on various government welfare schemes for senior citizens.

The programme was graced by Ms Tshering Doma Bhutia, Counsellor, MNP, as the Chief Guest, and Shri Anant Jain, IAS, District Collector, Mangan, as the Special Guest. Their presence greatly encouraged the participants and underscored the importance of the initiative.
 

Resource persons from different departments delivered informative sessions. From the Health Department, Mr Ongyal Tshering Lepcha, ABDM Project Coordinator, along with officials from the District Hospital, 

including Ms Chusom Lepcha, generated awareness on ABHA ID, PMJAY, and the benefits of the ABHA Card. On-the-spot generation of ABHA Cards was facilitated for the participants. Mr Sonam Namgyal Bhutia, Nutrition Inspector, sensitised the senior citizens on balanced nutrition and healthy dietary practices in old age.

Social Welfare Officer highlighted various welfare schemes available for senior citizens under the Social Welfare Department. Ms Sonam Laden Lachungpa, DD-cum- CDPO, elaborated on the objectives of AVAY and shared practical guidance on maintaining health, safety, and security in later years. Addressing the gathering, Shri Anant Jain, IAS, DC Mangan, explained in detail the provisions of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, and encouraged senior citizens to remain active, informed, and healthy.

The Chief Guest expressed appreciation for the initiative and encouraged senior citizens to adopt healthy lifestyles and make effective use of government welfare schemes. The programme also included recreational activities and games for senior citizens, followed by distribution of gifts. The event concluded successfully with active participation and positive feedback from the beneficiaries.

Further, necessary documents like Aadhar Card, ration card were collected from the beneficiaries to ensure proper verification and for the distribution of free assistive equipments for the senior citizens.
Overall, the programme effectively achieved its objectives of awareness generation, health promotion, and encouragement of active ageing under the Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana.

descriptionHtml:
REPORT ON SENSITIZATION AND AWARENESS, INTERGENERATIONAL BONDING ACTIVITIES AND HEALTH & MEDICAL CAMP UNDER ATAL VAYO ABHYUDAYA YOJANA IN NAMCHI DISTRICT 

The Sensitization and Awareness programme for Senior Citizens of Namch District was successfully organised today on 12/03/2026 at Town Hall Namchi under the Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVAY), with the objective of promoting active ageing, health awareness and dissemination of information on various governmen welfare schemes for senior citizen.
The Programme was graced by Mr. Ganesh Rai, Counsellor, NMC as Chie Guest and Shri S D Kalikotey, SDM Ravangla as the Special Guest. Their presence added significance to the event and encouraged active participation among senio citizen.

The Mega Health Camp for Senior Citizen was organised on 09/03/2026 at the Namthang Block under the Atal Vayo Abhudaya Yojana. The programme was conducted by the Women, Child, Senior Citizen and Divyangjan Welfare Departmen with primary objective of promoting the health and well-being of senior citizen by providing accessible healthcare services at their door step and creating awarenes: regarding various welfare schemes and support systems available under the Department.

Resource persons from various departments delivered informative session: during the programme. Dietician from the Health Department sensitized the senio citizens on the importance of balance nutrition and healthy dietary practices in old age

Mr. Shyam S. Pradhan, Social Welfare Officer highlighted various departmenta schemes for the senior citizen and elaborated on the objectives of Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana and shared useful tips for maintaining good health, safety and security of senior citizen and also briefed the beneficiaries in detail about the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), Old Age Pension Schemes and other welfare initiative under state and central government programmes. An interactive session was conducted to address quarries and provide counselling regarding eligibility criteria, documentation requirements and procedural formalities for availing benefits. Senior Citizens were specially sensitised about the importance of maintaining essential documents such as Aadhaar Card, Ration Card, Voter ID and other relevant records necessary for various schemes.

The event successfully promoted inter-generational harmony, social inclusion and community bonding by walkathon along with the Senior Citizen and their Gran Children or the Children of the Child Care Institute on 07/03/2026 at Melli Block under the banner on Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana by the Women, Child, Senior Citizen and Divyangjan Welfare Department.
The Chief Guest Shri Ganesh Rai, expressed her gratuity to the organizing department for conducting such a meaningful and much needed programme. H encouraged the senior citizens to lead a healthy life style, consume nutritious food and make effective use of government welfare scheme.
 

Addressing the gathering. Shri S D Kalikotey, SCS, SDM, highlighted the welfare schemes available for senior citizen and explained the provisions of the Maintenance and welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 in detail. He urged senior citizens to remain active, informed and healthy.
The programme also featured recreational activities. The event concluded on a positive note with active participation and appreciation from the beneficiaries. Overall the programme was a great success and effectively met its objectives of awareness generation, health promotion and active ageing under Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana.

title: Sensitization & Awareness, Health & Medical Camp & Inte
location: St Xavier School Pakyong, Pakyong District, Pakyong, Sikkim
descriptionHtml:
The District Level Integrated Senior Citizens Welfare Programme was organised at St. Xavier’s School Ground, Pakyong District, by the Women, Child, Senior Citizen & Divyangjan Welfare Department under the framework of the Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana.
The programme aimed to promote the welfare, dignity, and active participation of senior citizens in society. It also focused on strengthening intergenerational bonding by involving students, volunteers, community members, and elderly participants on a common platform.
Objectives
i) To promote the physical, mental, and social well-being of senior citizens.
ii) To honour and recognise the valuable contributions of senior citizens.
iii) To create awareness about welfare schemes, legal rights, and services available for the elderly. 

iv) To encourage intergenerational bonding and community participation. Inaugural Session
 

The programme commenced with a welcome address by Ms. Dikit Lepcha, Deputy Director-cum- Social Welfare Officer (SWO), Women, Child, Senior Citizen & Divyangjan Welfare Department, who warmly welcomed the dignitaries and participants. In her address, she sensitised senior citizens on their rights, welfare provisions, and the importance of active participation in society. The significance and vision of the programme were highlighted by the District Collector, Rohan Agawane Ramesh, IAS, who emphasised the importance of preserving traditions, strengthening intergenerational relationships, and ensuring dignity and respect for senior citizens.
 

The programme was graced by the Hon’ble Chief Guest, Mrs. Pamin Lepcha, MLA of Gnathang- Machong Constituency and Advisor to the Women, Child, Senior Citizen & Divyangjan Welfare Department, along with senior district officials.
The event also witnessed the presence of the President and Executive Members of the Sikkim Government Retired Employees Welfare Association, Sikkim Senior Citizens Foundation, Sikkim Government Retired Teachers’ Welfare Association, and Panchayat Presidents of various GPUs, reflecting strong community participation and institutional support.
 

Programme Activities and Highlights
Participation and Felicitation:
Senior citizens from different parts of Pakyong District actively participated in the programme and were felicitated with tokens of appreciation in recognition of their lifelong service and contributions.
 

Legal Awareness Session:
Resource person Senior Advocate Mr. Narendra Rai from the Sikkim State Legal Services Authority (SLSA) delivered an informative session on the rights and welfare of senior citizens, elaborating on legal safeguards, maintenance provisions, and remedies available in cases of neglect or abuse.
Health Camp:
A medical team deputed by the Chief Medical Officer, Pakyong, organised a comprehensive health camp for senior citizens. The camp included screening and examination for non-communicable diseases (NCDs), dementia screening, oral hygiene assessment, and mental health evaluation, thereby promoting preventive healthcare and early diagnosis.

 

Walkathon cum Intergenerational Bonding:
A walkathon was organised by the SWO Office to promote the message of healthy and active ageing, encouraging senior citizens to adopt physically active lifestyles.
Composite Regional Centre, Assam Lingzey also participated in the programme.

Storytelling Session:
A storytelling session was conducted by senior citizen Mr Navin Dawari, highlighting oral traditions, life experiences, and cultural values passed down through generations, thereby strengthening intergenerational learning.
Book Launch:
The programme featured the launch of books authored by senior citizens, including Merger Memories & Other Stories by Hemant Gurung and the Lepcha novel Numkum by Nimkit Lepcha, celebrating literary contributions of the elderly.
Student Participation:
Students from various educational institutions across the district formed the core participants of the programme, actively engaging with senior citizens and fostering intergenerational bonding.
 

Outcome and Impact
The programme resulted in:
i) Increased awareness among senior citizens regarding welfare schemes and legal rights.
ii) Promotion of preventive healthcare and healthy ageing practices.
iii) Enhanced dignity, self-esteem, and social inclusion of senior citizens.
iv) Strengthened collaboration among the district administration, Welfare Department, medical authorities, civil society organisations, and educational institutions.
v) Reinforced intergenerational respect, understanding, and cultural continuity.
 

Conclusion:
The District Level Integrated Senior Citizens Welfare Programme was successfully conducted and received an overwhelming and encouraging response from senior citizens, stakeholders, and the community. The initiative effectively fulfilled its objectives by promoting active ageing, social inclusion, legal awareness, and dignity of senior citizens.
Through meaningful activities such as legal sensitisation, health screenings, walkathon, storytelling, and literary recognition, the programme created a holistic platform for empowerment and engagement of the elderly.
The initiative reaffirmed the commitment of the district administration and the Women, Child, Senior Citizen & Divyangjan Welfare Department towards ensuring the welfare, empowerment, and active participation of senior citizens in society, in alignment with the vision and objectives of the Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana.

title: Swachhta Abhiyan & Ek Ped Maa Kee Nam
location: Namchi Ranipool Rakdong Tintek, OAH Boomtar Namchi, OAH Ranipool, Desitute Home Tintek Lee Aal Sangh, Gangtok, Sikkim
descriptionHtml:
A Brief Report Sikkim Senior Citizens’ Foundation reaches out to Care Giving Centres in the State in coordination with Women, Child, Senior Citizen and Divyangjan Welfare Department, Government of Sikkim.
The Sikkim Senior Citizens’ Foundation, in coordination with Women, Child, Senior Citizen and Divyangjan Welfare Department, under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana conducted a Swachhta Abhiyan programme and Plantation drive under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ at two designated places on 17th and 18th October.
On 17th October, the President and Members of the Foundation participated in the cleanliness and plantation drive at Old Age Home, Boomtar, Namchi. The drive had the presence and participation of Shri KN Sharma, President SSCF, and Members Dr. Vijay Singhi, Shri Hem Chhetri, Shri GD Giri, Shri CN Sharma, Shri SS Timsina, along with Shri Shyam Pradhan Social Welfare Officer Namchi, Shri Passang Bhutia, Incharge, Old Age Home, Boomtar, and Inspectors, Women, Child, Senior Citizen & Divyagjan Welfare Department Namchi.
On 18th October, the Members of the Foundation carried out similar drive at Old Age Home, Saramsa, Ranipool. The President and Members of Sikkim Senior Citizens’ Foundation were joined by Shri Pemba Lepcha, Chief Engineer-cum-Nodal Officer, State Designated Agency, Power Department, Smt. Mani Kala Gurung, Social Welfare Officer, Gangtok, Smt. Asha Chettri Councilor Ranipool, Inspectors Women, Child, Senior Citizen & Divyangjan Welfare Department, Gangtok and Senior Citizens from Ranipool Area.
Along with the cleanliness and plantation drive, the Members of Sikkim Senior Citizen Foundation also held an awareness camp at both the venues to educate the participants comprising senior citizens from the areas on Maintenance of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007.
Likewise, the Sikkim Senior Citizens’ Foundation, in coordination with Women, Child, Senior Citizen and Divyangjan Welfare Department, under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana conducted a Plantation drive under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ programme at Lee Aal Destitute Home in Upper Rakdong under Tumin Lingee constituency on 26th October, 2025.
The team, led by Shri KN Sharma, President SSCF, and accompanied by Members Dr. Vijay Singhi, Shri Hem Kumar Chhetri, Shri GD Giri and other members visited the Destitute Home and handed over essential items like rice, dal, edible oil etc. The items were handed over to Smt Passangkit Lepcha, the incharge of the Destitute Home, in the presence of the residents. The centre houses a total of 26 residents, EntBi comprising 9 females and 17 males.
The drive was part of the ongoing in initiative of Sikkim Senior Citizens’ Foundation to address the genuine needs of care giving centres, especially senior citizens, and spread awareness about the rights of Senior Citizens under the relevant Act.

title: State level consultation meeting on care economy
location: Ambedkar Bhawan Jaipur, ambedkar bhawan jaipur, Jaipur, Rajasthan
descriptionHtml:
A State-Level Consultation Meeting on the Care Economy was organised  by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment. The meeting was chaired by Shri Dinesh Kumar, Additional Chief Secretary, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment.

Officers from various departments of the State Government, representatives of non-governmental organisations, development partner institutions, and other stakeholders associated with the care sector actively participated in the meeting.

On this occasion, Shri Lalit Kumar, Director and Joint Secretary, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, informed that the objective of the meeting was to obtain suggestions and recommendations from various departments and stakeholders for strengthening and developing an inclusive care economy in the State.

He informed that detailed discussions were held on the major challenges faced at the field level in relation to the Care Economy, possible solutions to these challenges, and measures for making care services more effective and accessible. Discussions were also held on successful models, innovations and best practices being implemented in the State that have the potential to be scaled up and replicated at the national level.

Shri Lalit Kumar further informed that extensive deliberations were held on policy and implementation recommendations for strengthening the Care Economy system. Participants shared their suggestions on important aspects such as institutional arrangements, financial resources, skill development, service delivery mechanisms, convergence among various departments, and effective monitoring systems.

He added that all the suggestions and recommendations received during the consultation meeting would be compiled and forwarded to the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, for consideration in the formulation of policies and future action plans related to the Care Economy at the national level.

Chairing the meeting, Shri Dinesh Kumar, Additional Chief Secretary, highlighted the importance of the Care Economy and emphasised the need for effective coordination and convergence among various departments and stakeholders. He stressed the importance of strengthening quality and accessible care services for women, children, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, and other sections requiring care and support.

The meeting witnessed active participation from officers of various departments, representatives of non-governmental organisations, and other stakeholders, who presented valuable suggestions and recommendations for strengthening the Care Economy ecosystem.

descriptionHtml: The Women, Child, Senior Citizen and Divyangjan Welfare Department has disseminated an awareness message through various social media platforms regarding the provisions of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 and the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Rules, 2007. The initiative was undertaken with the objective of spreading awareness among the general public about the rights, protection, care, and welfare of senior citizens and parents. The Act emphasizes the responsibility of children and relatives to provide proper maintenance and support to elderly parents and senior citizens, ensuring that they live with dignity, safety, and respect in society. Through this awareness campaign, the department urged citizens to extend compassion, care, and emotional support towards the elderly and to promote a culture of respect and responsibility within families and communities. The department further highlighted the importance of safeguarding the welfare and well-being of senior citizens and encouraged everyone to actively contribute towards building an inclusive, caring, and age-friendly society.

title: Workshop on welfare and empowerment of senior citizens
location: Jaipur, Indira gandhi Panchayati raj and gramin vikas sansthan Gandhi nagar Jaipur, Rajasthan
descriptionHtml:
A workshop on  Empowerment and Welfare of Senior Citizens was successfully organized at  Indira Gandhi Panchayati Raj and Gramin Vikas Sansthan, Jaipur. Program included sessions on yoga and meditation, mental health, nutrition, social security benefits, prevention of elder abuse, financial planning, and social engagement.

Approximately 350 senior citizens participated in the workshop and benefitted from the informative sessions and interactive activities conducted throughout the day.

title: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day
location: Syrighat Solan, Syrighat, Tehsil Solan District Solan Himachal Pradesh, Solan, Himachal Pradesh
descriptionHtml:
The State Level programme on the occasion of World Elder Abuse Awareness Day was observed on 15th June 2026 at Syrighat District Solan in which total 350 participants were participated. 

Further, the Hon’ble Minister (SJ&E) was preside over as Chief Guest on the occasion and the special activities as listed below was organized during the occasion.  

  • Pledge campaigns against elder abuse.
  • Legal awareness on the provision of the Himachal Pradesh Maintenance of Parents and Dependants Act, 2001.
  • Health Check-up camp for the Senior Citizens.
  • Cultural programmes, debates, essay competitions and poster-making activities on respect and care for elders.
  • Talk on inter-generational bounding 
  • ALICMO Camps under Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana.

title: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day
location: Dr Ambedkar Bhawan Sector twelve, Dr Ambedkar Bhawan, Sec-12, Gandhinagar, Gandhinagar, Gujarat
descriptionHtml: Elder-line Gujarat c/o HelpAge India and Social Justice for Women and Child welfare department Gujarat as organised a joint awareness program for senior citizens of Gandhinagar as part of Elder Abuse day. nearly 184 senior citizens attended the event. Event was attended by Smt Miraben Patel Mayor Gandhinagar, Mr. Shital Gurjar Sir Dy Sp Nodel SDRF, Ms Shital Raval Probation officer from Social Justice and Empowerment and Dr Parth Goswami Health Officer Gandhinagar. More then 184 senior citizens marked their attendance in this event from 4 different Senior Citizens Associations of Gandhinagar. World Elder Abuse Awareness Day was initiated by the International Network for the Prevention of Elder Abuse (INPEA) and officially recognized as a UN day by the United Nations General.

title: youth generations connect a day of joy, games, and resp
location: Barmer, khudala barmer, Rajasthan
organizer: Social Justice and Empowerment Department jaipur
descriptionHtml: Senior and Youth Connect Programme was organized to promote meaningful interaction and strengthen the bond between senior citizens and youth participants. Various activities were organized, including awareness sessions, plantation drives, health and hygiene programmes, community service, cultural events, and yoga sessions. Youth and senior citizens actively participated together in these activities, fostering mutual respect, empathy, and social harmony. The programme provided valuable learning experiences while encouraging community engagement and intergenerational understanding.
